bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第192卷卷第一百九十二

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 192, the one hundred ninety-second juan.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 192

sentences.zh: 【唐紀八】 起柔兆閹茂九月，盡著雍困敦七月，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 8] Beginning in the ninth month of Rouzhao Xianmao, ending in the seventh month of Zhuoyong Kundun, two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 8] From the ninth month of Rouzhao Xianmao through the seventh month of Zhuoyong Kundun—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 九月，突厥頡利獻馬三千匹，羊萬口；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Türk qaghan Jieli presented three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Türk qaghan Jieli presented three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep;

sentences.zh: 上不受，但詔歸所掠中國戶口，征溫彥博還朝。

translations.literal: the Emperor did not accept them, but only ordered the return of Chinese subjects who had been carried off in raids and summoned Wen Yanbo back to court.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor declined the gifts and instead ordered the return of Chinese subjects taken in raids and summoned Wen Yanbo back to court.

sentences.zh: 丁未，上引諸衛將卒習射於顯德殿庭，諭之曰：「戎狄侵盜，自古有之，患在邊境少安，則人主逸游忘戰，是以寇來莫之能御。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Emperor led generals and soldiers of the guard units to practice archery in the courtyard of Xiande Hall and instructed them, saying: "Raids and plunder by the Rong and Di have existed since antiquity; the trouble is that when the frontier is briefly at peace, rulers indulge in pleasure and forget warfare, so that when invaders come none can resist them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the emperor led guard officers and troops to practice archery in the courtyard of Xiande Hall and addressed them: "Barbarian raids are as old as history itself; the danger is that when the border is briefly quiet, rulers grow idle and forget war, and then no one can hold the line when enemies strike.

sentences.zh: 今朕不使汝曹穿池築苑，專習弓矢，居閒無事，則為汝師，突厥入寇，則為汝將，庶幾中國之民可以少安乎！」

translations.literal: Now I do not have you dig ponds and build parks, but devote yourselves solely to bow and arrow; when at leisure with nothing to do, I will be your teacher; when the Türks invade, I will be your general—perhaps the people of China may enjoy a little peace!"
translations.idiomatic: I will not have you dig ponds and build pleasure grounds; you are to train only with bow and arrow. In peacetime I will be your instructor; when the Türks invade, I will be your commander—so that the people of China may know a little peace!"

sentences.zh: 於是日引數百人教射於殿庭，上親臨試，中多者賞以弓、刀、帛，其將帥亦加上考。

translations.literal: Thereupon each day he brought several hundred men to the hall courtyard to teach archery; the Emperor personally supervised the trials, and those who hit the target most often were rewarded with bows, blades, and silk; their commanders also received superior merit ratings.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he brought several hundred men to the hall each day for archery drill. The emperor personally supervised the trials; those who scored the most hits received bows, blades, and silk, and their commanders earned top merit ratings as well.

sentences.zh: 群臣多諫曰：「於律，以兵刃至御在所者絞。

translations.literal: Many ministers remonstrated, saying: "By law, bringing weapons to the imperial presence is punishable by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers remonstrated: "By law, anyone who brings weapons into the imperial presence is liable to execution by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 今使卑碎之人張弓挾矢於軒陛之側，陛下親在其間，萬一有狂夫竊發，出於不意，非所以重社稷也。」

translations.literal: Now you have low and humble men drawing bows and holding arrows beside the imperial steps, with Your Majesty among them; should some madman strike unexpectedly, that is no way to honor the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you now have common soldiers with bows drawn beside the imperial steps, and Your Majesty stands among them. Should some madman strike without warning, that is no way to safeguard the realm."

sentences.zh: 韓州刺史封同人詐乘驛馬入朝切諫。

translations.literal: The prefect of Hanzhou, Feng Tongren, feigned use of a post-horse to enter the capital and remonstrate urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Tongren, prefect of Hanzhou, abused the post-horse relay to rush to court and plead urgently against the practice.

sentences.zh: 上皆不聽，曰：「王者視四海如一家，封域之內，皆朕赤子，朕一一推心置其腹中，奈何宿衛之士亦加猜忌乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor would not heed any of them and said: "A true king regards the four seas as one household; within his domain all are his children. I place my heart in each of their breasts—why should I also be suspicious of the men who guard my sleep?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen. He said: "A true king treats the four seas as one household; everyone within his realm is his child. I trust each of them with my whole heart—why should I suspect the very men who guard my sleep?"

sentences.zh: 由是人思自勵，數年之間，悉為精銳。

translations.literal: Because of this, men strove to excel themselves, and within a few years all became crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Inspired by this, the men drove themselves to excel, and within a few years they had all become crack troops.

sentences.zh: 上嘗言：「吾自少經略四方，頗知用兵之要，每觀敵陳，則知其強弱，常以吾弱當其強，強當其弱。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "From youth I have campaigned in all directions and know fairly well the essentials of using troops. Whenever I observe the enemy's battle line, I know where it is strong and weak; I always match our weak points against their strong points and our strong points against their weak points.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once remarked: "Since youth I have campaigned across the realm and know the essentials of war. Whenever I study the enemy's line, I see where it is strong and where it is weak; I always pit our weakness against their strength and our strength against their weakness.

sentences.zh: 彼乘吾弱，逐奔不過數十百步，吾乘其弱，必出其陳後反擊之，無不潰敗，所以取勝，多在此也。」

translations.literal: When they exploit our weakness and pursue a retreat, they advance no more than several tens or hundreds of paces; when we exploit their weakness, we always strike from behind their line and counterattack—none fail to collapse in defeat. Most of my victories have come from this."
translations.idiomatic: When they press our weak flank, their pursuit rarely carries more than a few dozen or hundred paces; when we press their weak flank, we always wheel behind their line and counterattack, and they invariably break. Most of my victories have come from this."

sentences.zh: 己酉，上面定勳臣長孫無忌等爵邑，命陳叔達於殿下唱名示之，且曰：「朕敘卿等勳賞或未當，宜各自言。」

translations.literal: On jiyou, the Emperor finalized the titles and fiefs of meritorious ministers such as Zhangsun Wuji, ordered Chen Shuda to call out their names below the hall and show them, and said: "In ranking your merits and rewards I may not have got it right; each of you should speak up."
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the emperor finalized ranks and fiefs for meritorious ministers including Zhangsun Wuji, had Chen Shuda read out their names in the hall below, and said: "I may not have ranked your merits correctly—speak up if you think otherwise."

sentences.zh: 於是諸將爭功，紛紜不已。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals disputed over merit without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The generals at once began wrangling over who deserved more credit.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通曰：「臣舉兵關西，首應義旗，今房玄齡，杜如晦等專弄刀筆，功居臣上，臣竊不服。」

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Li Shentong said: "Your subject raised troops in Guanxi and was first to answer the banner of righteousness; now Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui wield only the brush yet rank above me—I cannot in my heart accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Li Shentong said: "I raised troops in Guanxi and was first to answer the righteous banner, yet Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui, who wield only the brush, rank above me—I cannot accept that."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「義旗初起，叔父雖首唱舉兵，蓋亦自營脫禍。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When the righteous banner first rose, Uncle, though you were first to call for arms, you were chiefly securing your own escape from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When the righteous cause first arose, Uncle, you were indeed first to raise troops—but chiefly to save yourself.

sentences.zh: 及竇建德吞噬山東，叔父全軍覆沒；

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande swallowed Shandong, Uncle, your entire army was destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande overran Shandong, your entire army was wiped out;

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥再合餘燼，叔父望風奔北。

translations.literal: when Liu Heita gathered the embers again, Uncle, you fled north at the mere sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Heita rallied the remnants, you fled north at the first sign of trouble.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等運籌帷幄，坐安社稷，論功行賞，固宜居叔父之先。

translations.literal: Xuanling and the others plotted within the tent and secured the altars of state while seated; in weighing merit and granting reward, they rightly belong before Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and his colleagues plotted strategy from headquarters and secured the realm without leaving their seats; in merit and reward they rightly come before you.

sentences.zh: 叔父，國之至親，朕誠無所愛，但不可以私恩濫與勳臣同賞耳！」

translations.literal: Uncle, you are the state's closest kin; I truly hold back nothing in affection, but private favor must not be lavished so that you share reward on equal terms with meritorious ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: You are the state's closest kinsman, and I withhold no private affection—but private favor must not let you share equal reward with those who earned it on merit!"

sentences.zh: 諸將乃相謂曰：「陛下至公，雖淮安王尚無所私，吾儕何敢不安其分。」

translations.literal: The generals then said to one another: "His Majesty is utterly fair—even Prince Huai'an received no favoritism; how dare we not be content with our stations?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals then said among themselves: "His Majesty is utterly fair—even Prince Huai'an won no favoritism. How can we fail to accept our due?"

sentences.zh: 遂皆悅服。

translations.literal: They all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: They all submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡嘗言：「秦府舊人未遷官者，皆嗟怨曰：『吾屬奉事左右，幾何年矣！

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling once said: "Former men of the Prince of Qin's household who have not yet been promoted all sigh in resentment, saying: 'We have served at Your Majesty's side—how many years now!
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling once reported: "Former staff of the Prince of Qin's household who have not yet been promoted complain: 'We have served at Your Majesty's side for years!

sentences.zh: 今除官，返出前宮、齊府人之後。』」

translations.literal: Now when offices are granted, we are placed after men from the former Eastern Palace and the Prince of Qi's household.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yet when appointments are made, we are ranked below men from the former Eastern Palace and the Prince of Qi's household.'"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「王者至公無私，故能服天下之心。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "A true king is utterly fair and without private bias, and thereby wins the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A true king is utterly impartial, and thereby wins the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕與卿輩日所衣食，皆取諸民者也。

translations.literal: What you and I eat and wear each day is all taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: What you and I eat and wear each day comes from the people.

sentences.zh: 故設官分職，以為民也，當擇賢才而用之，豈以新舊為先後哉！

translations.literal: Therefore offices and duties are established for the people's sake; one should select the worthy and employ them—how can seniority of service set the order!
translations.idiomatic: Offices exist for the people's sake; appoint the able, regardless of how long they have served you—how can old ties set the order!

sentences.zh: 必也新而賢，舊而不肖，安可捨新而取舊乎！

translations.literal: If the new are worthy and the old unworthy, how can one abandon the new and take the old!
translations.idiomatic: If newcomers are able and veterans unfit, how can I favor the old over the new!

sentences.zh: 今不論其賢不肖而直言嗟怨，豈為政之體乎！」

translations.literal: Now to complain without regard to worth or unworthiness—is that the way to govern!"
translations.idiomatic: To complain without regard to merit—is that how a ruler should govern!"

sentences.zh: 詔：「民間不得妄立妖祠。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The people must not recklessly establish heterodox shrines.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Private heterodox shrines are forbidden among the people.

sentences.zh: 自非卜筮正術，其餘雜占，悉從禁絕。」

translations.literal: Apart from orthodox divination by milfoil and tortoise shell, all other miscellaneous prognostication is utterly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from orthodox milfoil and tortoise divination, all other forms of fortune-telling are banned."

sentences.zh: 上於弘文殿聚四部書二十餘萬卷，置弘文館於殿側，精選天下文學之士虞世南、褚亮、姚思廉、歐陽詢、蔡允恭、蕭德言等，以本官兼學士，令更日宿直，聽朝之隙，引入內殿，講論前言往行，商榷政事，或至夜分乃罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor at Hongwen Hall assembled more than two hundred thousand juan from the four bibliographic categories, established the Hongwen Institute beside the hall, carefully selected literary men of the realm—Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, Yao Silian, Ouyang Xun, Cai Yungong, Xiao Deyan, and others—appointing them scholars in addition to their regular posts, ordering them to take turns lodging on duty; in the intervals of court audiences he brought them into the inner hall to discuss words and deeds of former ages and weigh current affairs, sometimes not dismissing them until deep into the night.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongwen Hall the emperor assembled more than two hundred thousand volumes from the four bibliographic categories and established the Hongwen Institute beside it. He selected leading scholars of the realm—Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, Yao Silian, Ouyang Xun, Cai Yungong, Xiao Deyan, and others—as concurrent academicians on rotating night duty. Between audiences he summoned them to the inner hall to discuss the words and deeds of antiquity and debate current policy, sometimes keeping them until deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 又取三品已上子孫充弘文館學生。

translations.literal: He also took descendants of officials of the third rank and above to serve as students of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He also enrolled sons and grandsons of officials of the third rank and above as students at the institute.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day bingchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon of bingchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔追封故太子建成為息王，謚曰隱；

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed the former Crown Prince Li Jiancheng as Prince Xi, with posthumous title Yin;
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed the former crown prince Li Jiancheng as Prince Xi, posthumous title Yin;

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉為剌王，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: the Prince of Qi Li Yuanji as Prince La, and had them reburied according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: and the Prince of Qi Li Yuanji as Prince La, and had them reburied with full rites.

sentences.zh: 葬日，上哭之於宜秋門，甚哀。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the Emperor wept for them at Yiqiu Gate, deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day the emperor wept for them at Yiqiu Gate with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 魏徵、王珪表請陪送至墓所，上許之，命宮府舊僚皆送葬。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng and Wang Gui memorialized asking to accompany the coffins to the graves; the Emperor granted it and ordered all former staff of the palaces to attend the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng and Wang Gui asked to accompany the coffins to the graves; the emperor agreed and ordered all former palace staff to attend.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，立皇子中山王承乾為太子，生八年矣。

translations.literal: On guihai, the Emperor installed his son, Prince of Zhongshan Li Chengqian, as crown prince; he was eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the emperor installed his son, Prince of Zhongshan Li Chengqian, as crown prince; the boy was eight years old.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，初定功臣實封有差。

translations.literal: On gengchen, actual fiefs for meritorious ministers were first fixed at differing levels.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, actual fief incomes for meritorious ministers were first graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭瑀薦封德彝於上皇，上皇以為中書令。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yu had recommended Feng Deyi to the retired Emperor, who appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yu had recommended Feng Deyi to the retired emperor, who made him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，蕭瑀為左僕射，德彝為右僕射。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, Xiao Yu became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Deyi Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor acceded, Xiao Yu became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Deyi Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 議事已定，德彝數反之於上前，由是有隙。

translations.literal: After policy was settled, Deyi often reversed himself before the Emperor, and thereby a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: After decisions were made, Deyi often reversed himself before the emperor, and a rift grew between them.

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡、杜如晦新用事，皆疏瑀而親德彝，蕭瑀不能平，遂上封事論之，辭指寥落，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: At the time Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had newly come to power; both kept Xiao Yu at a distance while drawing close to Deyi. Xiao Yu could not accept this and submitted a sealed memorial on the matter; its arguments were sparse, and thereby he offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had lately risen to power; both kept Xiao Yu at arm's length while cultivating Deyi. Xiao Yu could not stomach this and submitted a sealed memorial; its arguments were thin, and he offended the throne.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀與陳叔達忿爭於上前，庚辰，瑀、叔達皆坐不敬，免官。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda quarreled angrily before the Emperor; on gengchen both were convicted of disrespect and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda quarreled angrily before the emperor; on gengchen both were convicted of disrespect and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 甲申，民部尚書裴矩奏「民遭突厥暴踐者，請戶給絹一匹。」

translations.literal: On jiashen, Minister of Revenue Pei Ju memorialized: "People who suffered Türk violence and trampling—please grant one bolt of silk per household."
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Minister of Revenue Pei Ju proposed: "For households ravaged by Türk raids, grant one bolt of silk per household."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕以誠信御下，不欲虛有存恤之名而無其實，戶有大小，豈得雷同給賜乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I rule my subjects with sincerity and trust and do not wish to have the name of relief without the reality. Households differ in size—how can the same grant be given to all alike!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I rule by sincerity and trust; I will not offer relief in name only. Households differ in size—how can one grant fit all alike!"

sentences.zh: 於是計口為率。

translations.literal: Thereupon relief was calculated by head count.
translations.idiomatic: Relief was therefore calculated per capita.

sentences.zh: 初，上皇欲強宗室以鎮天下，故皇再從、三從弟及兄弟之下，雖童孺皆為王，王者數十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, the retired Emperor wished to strengthen the imperial clan to secure the realm, so that younger cousins once and twice removed and all brothers' descendants, even children, were made princes—several dozen princes in all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the retired emperor had sought to strengthen the imperial clan to secure the realm; cousins and brothers' descendants, even infants, were made princes—several dozen in all.

sentences.zh: 上從容問群臣：「遍封宗子，於天下利乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor casually asked his ministers: "Does enfeoffing clansmen universally benefit the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor casually asked his ministers: "Does enfeoffing clansmen across the board benefit the realm?"

sentences.zh: 封德彝對曰：「前世唯皇子及兄弟乃為王，自餘非有大功，無為王者。

translations.literal: Feng Deyi replied: "In former ages only imperial sons and brothers were made kings; the rest received kingship only for great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi replied: "In former ages only imperial sons and brothers became kings; others received that rank only for great merit.

sentences.zh: 上皇敦睦九族，大封宗室，自兩漢以來未有如今之多者。

translations.literal: The retired Emperor cultivated harmony among the nine agnatic groups and enfeoffed the clan on a grand scale—since the Two Han there have been none so numerous as now.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor cultivated the nine agnatic groups and enfeoffed the clan on a grand scale—since the Han there have been none so numerous.

sentences.zh: 爵命既崇，多給力役，恐非示天下以至公也。」

translations.literal: Titles and appointments are already exalted and corvée labor is lavishly supplied— I fear this is not how to show the realm utmost fairness."
translations.idiomatic: Ranks are already lofty and corvée burdens heavy—I fear that is not how to show the realm true fairness."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 朕為天子，所以養百姓也，豈可勞百姓以養己之宗族乎！」

translations.literal: I am Son of Heaven in order to nourish the hundred surnames—how can I burden the people to nourish my own clan!"
translations.idiomatic: I am Son of Heaven to nourish the people—how can I burden the people to feed my own clan!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚寅，降宗室郡王皆為縣公，惟有功者數人不降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengyin, all clansmen who had been princes of commanderies were reduced to county marquises; only a few who had merit were not demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengyin, clansmen who had held princely commandery titles were reduced to county marquises; only a few with outstanding merit kept their ranks.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上與群臣論止盜。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Emperor discussed stopping theft with his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the emperor discussed how to stop theft with his ministers.

sentences.zh: 或請重法以禁之，上哂之曰：「民之所以為盜者，由賦繁役重，官吏貪求，饑寒切身，故不暇顧廉恥耳。

translations.literal: Some asked that severe laws be used to forbid it; the Emperor smiled and said: "The reason the people become thieves is that taxes are heavy and corvée burdensome, officials are greedy in their demands, and hunger and cold press upon their persons—therefore they have no leisure to consider shame.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged harsher laws; the emperor smiled and said: "People steal because taxes are heavy, corvée is crushing, officials extort them, and hunger and cold leave no room for shame.

sentences.zh: 朕當去奢省費，輕徭薄賦，選用廉吏，使民主食有餘，則自不為盜，安用重法邪！」

translations.literal: I should discard extravagance and economize expenditure, lighten corvée and reduce taxes, select and employ honest officials, and enable the people to have food in surplus—then they will not steal of themselves; what need is there for severe laws!"
translations.idiomatic: I will cut extravagance, lighten burdens, appoint honest officials, and see that people have food to spare—then they will not steal. What need is there for harsh laws!"

sentences.zh: 自是數年之後，海內昇平，路不拾遺，外戶不閉，商旅野宿焉。

translations.literal: From this, after several years peace prevailed within the seas; no one picked up lost objects on the road, outer gates were left unbarred, and merchants lodged in the open countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the realm was at peace: lost goods lay untouched on the roads, outer gates stood unbarred, and travelers slept in the open without fear.

sentences.zh: 上又嘗謂侍臣曰：「君依於國，國依於民。

translations.literal: The Emperor also once told his attendants: "The ruler depends on the state, and the state depends on the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also told his attendants: "The ruler depends on the state, and the state depends on the people.

sentences.zh: 刻民以奉君，猶割肉以充腹，腹飽而身斃，君富而國亡。

translations.literal: Carving out the people to serve the ruler is like cutting flesh to fill the belly—the belly is full but the body perishes; the ruler is rich but the state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the people to enrich the ruler is like cutting flesh to fill one's belly—the belly grows full while the body dies; the ruler grows rich while the realm perishes.

sentences.zh: 故人君之患，不自外來，常由身出。

translations.literal: Therefore the troubles of rulers do not come from without; they constantly arise from within themselves.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's ruin does not come from without; it arises from within.

sentences.zh: 夫欲盛則費廣，費廣則賦重，賦重則民愁，民愁則國危，國危則君喪矣。

translations.literal: When desires are lavish, expenditure is broad; when expenditure is broad, taxes are heavy; when taxes are heavy, the people are distressed; when the people are distressed, the state is endangered; when the state is endangered, the ruler is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant desire breeds heavy spending; heavy spending breeds heavy taxes; heavy taxes breed a desperate people; a desperate people breed a doomed state; and a doomed state breeds a dead ruler.

sentences.zh: 朕常以此思之，故不敢縱欲也。」

translations.literal: I constantly reflect on this, and therefore dare not indulge my desires."
translations.idiomatic: I reflect on this constantly, and therefore dare not indulge my desires."

sentences.zh: 十二月，己巳，益州大都督竇軌奏稱獠反，請發兵討之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jisi, the Grand Protector of Yizhou Dou Gui memorialized that the Liao had rebelled and asked to send troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jisi, Grand Protector of Yizhou Dou Gui reported that the Liao had rebelled and asked to send troops against them.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「獠依阻山林，時出鼠竊，乃其常俗；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Liao rely on mountain forests for refuge and from time to time emerge for petty theft—that is their ordinary custom;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Liao live in mountain fastnesses and raid like rats from time to time—that is their custom;

sentences.zh: 牧守苟能撫以恩信，自然帥服，安可輕動干戈，漁獵其民，比之禽獸，豈為民父母之意邪！」

translations.literal: if governors and protectors can soothe them with kindness and trust, they will naturally submit as leaders—how can one lightly move weapons of war and fish and hunt their people, treating them like birds and beasts—is that the mind of parents to the people!"
translations.idiomatic: if local officials treat them with kindness and trust, they will submit of their own accord. How can we lightly send armies to prey on them like game—is that how a parent treats the people!"

sentences.zh: 竟不許。

translations.literal: He ultimately did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: He refused permission.

sentences.zh: 上謂裴寂曰：「比多上書言事者，朕皆粘之屋壁，得出入省覽，每思治道，或深夜方寢。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Pei Ji: "Of late many have submitted memorials on affairs of state; I have pasted them all on the chamber walls so I can go in and out to review them. Whenever I ponder the way of governance I sometimes retire only deep into the night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Pei Ji: "Lately many memorials have arrived; I paste them on the walls of my chamber so I can review them coming and going. When I ponder how to govern, I sometimes sleep only deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 公輩亦當恪勤職業，副朕此意。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen should also diligently attend to your duties and match this intent of mine."
translations.idiomatic: You too must attend diligently to your duties and match my intent."

sentences.zh: 上厲精求治，數引魏徵入臥內，訪以得失；

translations.literal: The Emperor vigorously devoted himself to seeking good governance and repeatedly brought Wei Zheng into his sleeping quarters to inquire about successes and failures;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor devoted himself zealously to good governance and repeatedly summoned Wei Zheng to his private quarters to ask what was going right and wrong;

sentences.zh: 征知無不言，上皆欣然嘉納。

translations.literal: Zheng knew nothing he would not speak, and the Emperor gladly accepted all with praise.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng held nothing back, and the emperor gladly accepted every word.

sentences.zh: 上遣使點兵，封德彝奏：「中男雖未十八，其軀幹壯大者，亦可並點。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to muster troops; Feng Deyi memorialized: "Although middle youths are not yet eighteen, those whose frames are sturdy may also be mustered together."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to muster troops; Feng Deyi proposed: "Although 'middle youths' are under eighteen, those who are physically robust should be included in the levy."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 敕出，魏徵固執以為不可，不肯署敕，至於數四。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Wei Zheng stubbornly held it impossible and refused to countersign the edict, even to the fourth time.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was drafted, Wei Zheng firmly objected and refused to countersign it, repeating his refusal four times.

sentences.zh: 上怒，召而讓之曰：「中男壯大者，乃奸民詐妄以避征役，取之何害，而卿固執至此！」

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry, summoned him, and reproached him: "Sturdy middle youths are scoundrels who falsely claim exemption from levy and corvée—what harm in taking them, that you should be so stubborn to this point!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry, summoned him, and reproached him: "Robust middle youths are often frauds evading levy—what harm in drafting them, that you should be so stubborn!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「夫兵在御之得其道，不在眾多。

translations.literal: He replied: "Troops lie in governing them by the right way, not in being numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied: "Armies win by being led rightly, not by sheer numbers.

sentences.zh: 陛下取其壯健，以道御之，足以無敵於天下，何必多取細弱以增虛數乎！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty takes the robust and governs them by the right way, that is enough to be unmatched under Heaven—why must you take many weak ones to swell empty numbers!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty takes the fit and leads them well, you need no rival under Heaven—why swell the rolls with the weak and unfit!

sentences.zh: 且陛下每云：『吾以誠信御天下，欲使臣民皆無欺詐。』

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty often says: 'I rule all under Heaven with sincerity and trust and wish to make ministers and people free of deceit.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty often says: 'I rule by sincerity and trust and wish all subjects to be free of deceit.'

sentences.zh: 今即位未幾，失信者數矣！」

translations.literal: Yet since taking the throne it has not been long and there have already been several breaches of trust!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet since your accession you have already broken faith several times!"

sentences.zh: 上愕然曰：「朕何為失信？」

translations.literal: The Emperor started and said: "In what have I broken trust?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said: "How have I broken faith?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下初即位，下詔云：『逋負官物，悉令蠲免。』

translations.literal: He replied: "When Your Majesty first took the throne you issued an edict saying: 'Arrears of government goods are all ordered remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied: "When Your Majesty first acceded, you decreed: 'All arrears owed to government storehouses are remitted.

sentences.zh: 有司以為負秦府國司者，非官物，征督如故。

translations.literal: The responsible offices held that those who owed the Prince of Qin's household treasury were not government goods and collected as before.
translations.idiomatic: The offices held that debts to the Prince of Qin's household treasury were not government goods and collected them as before.

sentences.zh: 陛下以秦王升為天子，國司之物，非官物而何！

translations.literal: Your Majesty rose from Prince of Qin to Son of Heaven—are household treasury goods not government goods!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rose from Prince of Qin to Son of Heaven—are household treasury goods anything but government goods!

sentences.zh: 又曰：『關中免二年租調，關外給復一年。』

translations.literal: You also said: 'Within the passes, rent and corvée are exempted for two years; outside the passes, one year of relief is granted.'
translations.idiomatic: You also said: 'Within the passes, two years' rent and corvée are remitted; outside, one year of relief.'

sentences.zh: 既而繼有敕云：『已役已輸者，以來年為始。』

translations.literal: Soon afterward a further edict said: 'For those already levied and already paid, [exemption] begins from next year.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, another edict said: 'For those already levied or paid, relief begins next year.'

sentences.zh: 散還之後，方復更征，百姓固已不能無怪。

translations.literal: After the proclamation was sent out, collection was resumed— the people naturally could not be without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After the proclamation went out, collection resumed—the people naturally grumbled.

sentences.zh: 今既徵得物，復點為兵，何謂來年為始乎！

translations.literal: Now that goods have already been collected, you again muster them as soldiers—what does 'beginning from next year' mean!
translations.idiomatic: Now that payment has been taken, you draft them as soldiers—what does 'beginning next year' mean!

sentences.zh: 又，陛下所與共治天下者在於守宰，居常簡閱，鹹以委之；

translations.literal: Again, those with whom Your Majesty jointly govern the realm are the prefects and magistrates; you ordinarily review them carefully and entrust all to them;
translations.idiomatic: Again, those who govern the realm with you are the prefects and magistrates; you review them carefully and entrust all to them;

sentences.zh: 至於點兵，獨疑其詐，豈所謂以誠信為治乎！」

translations.literal: yet when it comes to mustering troops you alone suspect fraud—is that what is called governing by sincerity and trust!"
translations.idiomatic: yet in mustering troops you alone suspect fraud—is that governing by sincerity and trust!"

sentences.zh: 上悅曰：「向者朕以卿固執，疑卿不達政事，今卿論國家大體，誠盡其精要。

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "Earlier I took your stubbornness to mean you did not understand state affairs; now your discussion of the great principles of the state truly exhausts their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure: "I took your stubbornness to mean you did not understand statecraft; now your discussion of the great principles of governance truly hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 夫號令不信，則民不知所從，天下何由而治乎？

translations.literal: When commands are not trusted, the people do not know whom to follow—how can all under Heaven be governed!
translations.idiomatic: When commands are not trusted, the people do not know what to follow—how can the realm be governed!

sentences.zh: 朕過深矣！」

translations.literal: My fault runs too deep!"
translations.idiomatic: I have gone too far!"

sentences.zh: 乃不點中男，賜征金甕一。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not conscript youths of middle age and bestowed on Wei Zheng one golden jar.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he dropped the conscription of middle-aged youths and rewarded Wei Zheng with a golden jar.

sentences.zh: 上聞景州錄事參軍張玄素名，召見，問以政道，對曰：「隋主好自專庶務，不任群臣；

translations.literal: The Emperor heard the name of Zhang Xuansu, recording secretary of Jing Prefecture, summoned him, and questioned him on the way of governance. He replied: "The Sui emperor liked to monopolize all ordinary affairs himself and did not entrust his ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of Zhang Xuansu, recording secretary of Jing Prefecture, he summoned him and asked about the principles of governance. Zhang replied: "The Sui emperor liked to handle every detail of government himself and would not rely on his ministers;

sentences.zh: 群臣恐懼，唯知稟受奉行而已，莫之敢違。

translations.literal: the ministers were in fear, knowing only to receive orders and carry them out, none daring to disobey.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers lived in fear, knowing only how to receive orders and obey them, and none dared to defy him.

sentences.zh: 以一人之智決天下之務，借使得失相半，乖謬已多，下諛上蔽，不亡何待！

translations.literal: Using one man's wisdom to decide all affairs under Heaven—even granting gains and losses were half and half, errors would already be many; those below flatter while those above are blocked off—what wait for extinction!
translations.idiomatic: When one man's judgment decides the affairs of the entire realm, even if half his decisions were right, the mistakes would still be numerous; flattery below and blindness above—how could such a state avoid ruin!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能謹擇群臣而分任以事，高拱穆清而考其成敗以施刑賞，何憂不治！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly carefully select ministers and assign them duties, sit loftily in silent ease and examine their success and failure to apply punishments and rewards, why worry about failure to govern!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would carefully choose your ministers, delegate affairs to them, sit in dignified repose, and judge their success or failure when assigning rewards and punishments, why should you worry that the realm will not be well governed!

sentences.zh: 又，臣觀隋末亂離，其欲爭天下者不過十餘人而已，其餘皆保鄉黨、全妻子，以待有道而歸之耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant observes that amid the turmoil and division at the end of Sui, those who wished to contend for all under Heaven numbered no more than a dozen or so; the rest all protected their hometowns, preserved their wives and children, and awaited one possessed of the Way to whom they might submit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have observed that in the chaos at the end of the Sui, no more than a dozen men truly sought to seize the realm; the rest simply protected their communities, kept their families safe, and waited for a righteous ruler to whom they could submit.

sentences.zh: 乃知百姓好亂者亦鮮，但人主不能安之耳。」

translations.literal: Thus one knows that among the common people those who delight in chaos are also few—it is only that the ruler cannot settle them."
translations.idiomatic: This shows that few common people actually desire chaos; the problem is simply that rulers fail to give them peace."

sentences.zh: 上善其言，擢為侍御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and promoted him to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice and promoted him to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 前幽州記室直中書省張蘊古上《大寶箴》，其略曰：「聖人受命，拯溺亨屯，故以一人治天下，不以天下奉一人。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yungu, former secretary of You Prefecture now serving directly in the Secretariat, submitted the "Great Treasure Admonition," which in summary said: "The sage receives the Mandate, saves the drowning and brings ease to adversity; thus one man governs all under Heaven, and all under Heaven is not offered up to serve one man."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yungu, former secretary of You Prefecture and now a direct appointee in the Secretariat, submitted the "Great Treasure Admonition." In summary it said: "The sage receives Heaven's mandate, rescues the drowning and relieves hardship; therefore one man governs the realm, rather than the realm being made to serve one man."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「壯九重於內，所居不過容膝；

translations.literal: It also said: "He strengthens the ninefold palace within, yet what he inhabits need be no larger than enough to hold his knees;
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "The sage strengthens the inner palace, yet his dwelling need be no larger than a space to kneel in;

sentences.zh: 彼昏不知，瑤其台而瓊其室。

translations.literal: that benighted one does not know this and decks his terraces with jade and his chambers with fine gems.
translations.idiomatic: the benighted ruler knows nothing of this and decks his terraces in jade and his chambers in fine gems.

sentences.zh: 羅八珍於前，所食不過適口；

translations.literal: He spreads the eight delicacies before him, yet what he eats need be no more than enough to suit the mouth;
translations.idiomatic: He spreads the eight delicacies before him, yet eats only enough to satisfy his appetite;

sentences.zh: 惟狂罔念，丘其糟而池其酒。」

translations.literal: only the mad and unthinking one heaps up dregs and makes pools of wine."
translations.idiomatic: only the reckless and heedless ruler piles dregs into hills and turns wine into pools."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「勿沒沒而暗，勿察察而明，雖冕旒蔽目而視於未形，雖黈纊塞耳而聽於無聲。」

translations.literal: It also said: "Do not be obscure and dark; do not be finicky and overbright. Though the tassels of the crown veil the eyes, see what has not yet taken form; though the cotton plugs of the cap stop the ears, listen to what has no sound."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "Do not sink into obscurity, yet do not become finicky and overbearing. Though the crown's tassels veil the eyes, see what has not yet taken shape; though the cap's earplugs block the ears, listen to what makes no sound."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜以束帛，除大理丞。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended it, bestowed on him a bundle of silk, and appointed him assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial, rewarded him with silk, and appointed him assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 上召傅奕，賜之食，謂曰：「汝前所奏，幾為吾禍。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Fu Yi, gave him food, and said to him: "What you memorialized before nearly brought disaster upon me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Fu Yi, gave him a meal, and said: "Your earlier memorial nearly brought disaster upon me.

sentences.zh: 然凡有天變，卿宜盡言皆如此，勿以前事為懲也。」

translations.literal: Yet whenever there are celestial anomalies, you should speak out fully just as you did then, and do not take the earlier affair as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever there are celestial portents, you should speak as frankly as you did then, and do not let what happened before deter you."

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂奕曰：「佛之為教，玄妙可師，卿何獨不悟其理？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to Yi: "Buddhism as a teaching is profound and worthy to be taken as master—why alone do you not grasp its principle?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Fu Yi: "Buddhism is a profound teaching worthy of respect—why alone do you fail to see its truth?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「佛乃胡中桀黠，誑耀彼土。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Buddha was a cunning and crafty man among the barbarians, deceiving and dazzling that land.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The Buddha was a cunning charlatan among the barbarians, deceiving and dazzling that foreign land.

sentences.zh: 中國邪僻之人，取莊、老玄談，飾以妖幻之語，用欺愚俗。

translations.literal: Perverse men in China took the abstruse talk of Zhuangzi and Laozi, adorned it with sorcerous and illusory words, and used it to deceive the foolish masses.
translations.idiomatic: Perverse men in China took the abstruse doctrines of Zhuangzi and Laozi, dressed them in sorcerous language, and used them to deceive the common people.

sentences.zh: 無益於民，有害於國，臣非不悟，鄙不學也。」

translations.literal: It benefits the people in nothing and harms the state; your servant is not failing to grasp it—I disdain it and do not study it."
translations.idiomatic: It does the people no good and harms the state. It is not that I fail to understand it—I despise it and refuse to study it."

sentences.zh: 上頗然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor largely agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 上患吏多受賕，密使左右試賂之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled that many officials accepted bribes and secretly had his attendants test them with bribes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled by widespread official corruption and secretly sent his attendants to test officials with bribes.

sentences.zh: 有司門令史受絹一匹，上欲殺之，民部尚書裴矩諫曰：「為吏受賂，罪誠當死；

translations.literal: A clerk of the Department of Reception accepted one bolt of silk. The Emperor wished to execute him. Pei Ju, minister of the Ministry of Revenue, remonstrated, saying: "For an official to accept a bribe, the crime truly deserves death;
translations.idiomatic: A clerk in the Department of Reception accepted one bolt of silk. The emperor wanted to execute him, but Pei Ju, minister of the Ministry of Revenue, remonstrated: "An official who accepts a bribe surely deserves death;

sentences.zh: 但陛下使人遺之而受，乃陷人於法也，恐非所謂『道之以德，齊之以禮。』」

translations.literal: but Your Majesty had a man send it to him and he accepted it—this is entrapping a man in the law, and I fear this is not what is meant by 'guide them with virtue, harmonize them with ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: but when Your Majesty sends someone to offer a bribe and the man accepts it, you are entrapping him in the law. I fear this is not what is meant by 'guide them with virtue and harmonize them with ritual.'

sentences.zh: 上悅，召文武五品已上告之曰：「裴矩能當官力爭，不為面從，倘每事皆然，何憂不治！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased. He summoned civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above and told them: "Pei Ju can, in discharging his office, strive forcefully and not simply agree to one's face; if every matter were like this, why worry about failure to govern!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased. He summoned civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above and said: "Pei Ju can stand his ground in office and argue forcefully instead of simply agreeing to one's face. If every matter were handled this way, why should we worry that the realm will not be well governed!"

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：古人有言：君明臣直。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The ancients had a saying: when the ruler is enlightened, the minister is upright.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: The ancients said, "When the ruler is enlightened, the minister is upright."

sentences.zh: 裴矩佞於隋而忠於唐，非其性之有變也；

translations.literal: Pei Ju was sycophantic under Sui yet loyal under Tang—not because his nature had changed;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju was sycophantic under the Sui yet loyal under the Tang—not because his nature had changed,

sentences.zh: 君惡聞其過，則忠化為佞，君樂聞直言，則佞化為忠。

translations.literal: when the ruler hates to hear of his faults, loyalty turns into sycophancy; when the ruler delights to hear blunt speech, sycophancy turns into loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: but because when a ruler hates to hear of his faults, loyalty turns into sycophancy, and when a ruler welcomes blunt speech, sycophancy turns into loyalty.

sentences.zh: 是知君者表也，臣者景也，表動則景隨矣。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the ruler is the gnomon and the minister is the shadow; when the gnomon moves, the shadow follows.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the ruler is the gnomon and the minister is the shadow: when the gnomon moves, the shadow follows.

sentences.zh: 是歲，進皇子長沙郡王恪為漢王，宜陽郡王祐為楚王。

translations.literal: In this year, the princes were advanced in rank: Prince of Changsha Commandery, Ke, was made Prince of Han, and Prince of Yiyang Commandery, You, was made Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the emperor advanced his sons in rank: Li Ke, Prince of Changsha Commandery, was made Prince of Han, and Li You, Prince of Yiyang Commandery, was made Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 新羅、百濟、高麗三國有宿仇，迭相攻擊；

translations.literal: The three states of Silla, Baekje, and Goguryeo had old enmities and attacked one another in turn;
translations.idiomatic: Silla, Baekje, and Goguryeo had long-standing enmities and attacked one another in turn;

sentences.zh: 上遣國子助教朱子奢往諭指，三國皆上表謝罪。

translations.literal: the Emperor sent Zhu Zishe, assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education, to convey his instructions, and all three states submitted memorials apologizing.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor sent Zhu Zishe, assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education, to convey his instructions, and all three states submitted memorials of apology.

sentences.zh: 太宗文武大聖大廣孝皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Above, the first part of the reign of Emperor Taizong, the Cultured and Martial, Great Sage, Great Expansive Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang, the Cultured and Martial, Great Sage, Great Expansive Filial Emperor — Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiyou, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on yiyou, the first day of the first month, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上宴群臣，奏《秦王破陳樂》。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Emperor feasted his ministers and had the music "Prince of Qin Breaks Chen" performed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the emperor feasted his ministers and had the music "Prince of Qin Breaks Chen" performed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕昔受委專征，民間遂有此曲，雖非文德之雍容，然功業由茲而成，不敢忘本。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In the past I received commission for independent campaigning, and among the people this tune arose. Though it is not the easy grace of civil virtue, yet my achievements were accomplished through it, and I dare not forget my roots.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When I was entrusted with independent command in the field, this tune arose among the people. It is not the easy grace of civil virtue, yet my achievements were won through such deeds, and I dare not forget my roots.

sentences.zh: 封德彝曰：「陛下以神武平海內，豈文德之足比！」

translations.literal: Feng Deyi said: "Your Majesty, by divine martial prowess, pacified all within the seas—how can civil virtue be enough to compare!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi said: "Your Majesty pacified the realm through divine martial prowess—how can civil virtue alone compare!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「戡亂以武，守成以文，文武之用，各隨其時。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Quelling disorder is done with martial force; preserving achievement is done with civil virtue. The uses of civil and martial each follow their time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Disorder is quelled by force, achievement is preserved by civil virtue. Civil and martial power each has its proper season.

sentences.zh: 卿謂文不及武，斯言過矣。」

translations.literal: You say civil virtue does not reach martial force—this remark goes too far."
translations.idiomatic: To say that civil virtue falls short of martial force—that goes too far."

sentences.zh: 德彝頓首謝。

translations.literal: Deyi bowed his head to the ground in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 己亥，制：「自今中書、門下及三品以上入閣議事，皆命諫官隨之，有失輒諫。」

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict was issued: "From now on, whenever those of the Secretariat, Chancellery, and third rank and above enter the Inner Hall to deliberate on affairs, remonstrating officials shall be ordered to accompany them, and whenever there is fault they shall remonstrate at once."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, an edict was issued: "From now on, whenever officials of the Secretariat, Chancellery, and third rank and above enter the Inner Hall to deliberate on affairs, remonstrating officials shall accompany them and speak up immediately whenever they find fault."

sentences.zh: 上命吏部尚書長孫無忌等與學士、法官更議定律令，寬絞刑五十條為斷右趾，上猶嫌其慘，曰：「肉刑廢已久，宜有以易之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, together with academicians and judicial officials, to reconsider and fix the laws and ordinances. Fifty articles of strangulation were commuted to amputation of the right foot. The Emperor still considered this cruel and said: "Corporal punishments have long been abolished; there ought to be something to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, together with academicians and judicial officials, to revise the laws and ordinances. Fifty capital offenses that had carried strangulation were commuted to amputation of the right foot, but the emperor still found the punishment too harsh and said: "Corporal punishments were abolished long ago; we should find something to replace them.

sentences.zh: 蜀王法曹參軍裴弘獻請改為加役流，流三千里，居作三年；

translations.literal: Pei Hongxian, legal bureau aide of the Prince of Shu, submitted a request to change it to penal servitude added to exile—exile three thousand li, labor service for three years;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hongxian, legal bureau aide of the Prince of Shu, proposed replacing it with penal servitude added to exile: exile three thousand li, with three years of compulsory labor;

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: an edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor approved the proposal by edict.

sentences.zh: 上以兵部郎中戴冑忠清公直，擢為大理少卿。

translations.literal: Because Dai Zhou, bureau director of the Ministry of War, was loyal, pure, and fair, the Emperor promoted him to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dai Zhou, bureau director of the Ministry of War, was loyal, upright, and fair, the emperor promoted him to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 上以選人多詐冒資廕，敕令自首，不首者死。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because many candidates falsely claimed hereditary privilege, ordered them to confess voluntarily; those who did not confess would die.
translations.idiomatic: Because many examination candidates had falsely claimed hereditary privilege, the emperor ordered them to confess; those who did not would be executed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有詐冒事覺者，上欲殺之。

translations.literal: Before long, cases of false claims were discovered, and the Emperor wished to execute the offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, cases of fraud were discovered, and the emperor wanted to execute the offenders.

sentences.zh: 冑奏：「據法應流。」

translations.literal: Zhou memorialized: "According to the law, they should be exiled."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou memorialized: "Under the law, they should be sentenced to exile."

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「卿欲守法而使朕失信乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily said: "Do you wish to uphold the law and thereby make me break faith?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said: "Do you wish to uphold the law and make me break my word?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「敕者出於一時之喜怒，法者國家所以布大信於天下也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Edicts arise from momentary anger or pleasure; the law is what the state uses to spread great trust throughout all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Edicts arise from momentary anger or pleasure, but the law is how the state establishes lasting trust throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下忿選人之多詐，故欲殺之，而既知其不可，復斷之以法，此乃忍小忿而存大信也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, angered by the many frauds among candidates, therefore wished to kill them; yet now that you know this cannot be done and again decide the matter by law, this is enduring a small resentment in order to preserve great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, angered by the many frauds among candidates, wished to execute them; but now that you see this cannot stand and decide the matter according to law instead, you are restraining a small anger in order to preserve great public trust.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿能執法，朕復何憂！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If you can uphold the law, what further worry have I!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If you can uphold the law, what have I to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 冑前後犯顏執法，言如湧泉，上皆從之，天下無冤獄。

translations.literal: Zhou, time and again braving displeasure to uphold the law, spoke like a gushing spring, and the Emperor followed him in all cases; throughout the realm there were no unjust imprisonments.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou repeatedly braved the emperor's displeasure to uphold the law, speaking with unstoppable force, and the emperor accepted his judgments in every case; throughout the realm there were no wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 上令封德彝舉賢，久無所舉。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Feng Deyi to recommend worthy men, but for a long time he recommended none.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Feng Deyi to recommend worthy men, but for a long time Feng recommended no one.

sentences.zh: 上詰之，對曰：「非不盡心，但於今未有奇才耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned him. He replied: "It is not that I have not done my utmost, but at present there are simply no extraordinary talents."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him. Feng replied: "It is not that I have failed to do my utmost, but at present there simply are no extraordinary talents."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「君子用人如器，各取所長，古之致治者，豈借才於異代乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The superior man uses men as vessels, each taking what he excels at. Did the ancients who brought order borrow talent from another age?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A wise ruler uses men as tools, taking each for what he does best. Did the great rulers of antiquity borrow talent from another age?

sentences.zh: 正患己不能知，安可誣一世之人！」

translations.literal: The trouble is simply that one cannot recognize them—how can one slander all the men of an age!"
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is only that we fail to recognize talent—how can we dismiss an entire generation of men!"

sentences.zh: 德彝慚而退。

translations.literal: Deyi withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫杜淹奏「諸司文案恐有稽失，請令御史就司檢校。」

translations.literal: Du Yan, censor-in-chief, memorialized: "The documents of the various offices may contain delays and errors; I request that censors be sent to each office to inspect and verify them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan, censor-in-chief, memorialized: "The paperwork of the various offices may contain delays and errors. I request that censors be sent to each office to inspect and verify it.

sentences.zh: 上以問封德彝，對曰：「設官分職，各有所司。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Feng Deyi about this. He replied: "Offices are established and duties divided, each with its own charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Feng Deyi about the proposal. Feng replied: "Offices are established and duties divided, each with its own responsibility.

sentences.zh: 果有愆違，御史自應糾舉；

translations.literal: If there are truly faults and violations, the censors themselves ought to impeach them;
translations.idiomatic: If there are truly faults, the censors themselves should impeach the offenders;

sentences.zh: 若遍歷諸司，搜括疵纇，太為煩碎。」

translations.literal: if one goes through all the offices in turn, searching out flaws and defects, it is far too troublesome and petty."
translations.idiomatic: to go through every office in turn, searching out flaws and defects, would be excessively burdensome and petty."

sentences.zh: 淹默然。

translations.literal: Yan fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan fell silent.

sentences.zh: 上問淹：「何故不復論執？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Yan: "Why do you no longer press your argument?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Du Yan: "Why do you no longer press your argument?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天下之務，當盡至公，善則從之。

translations.literal: He replied: "Affairs under Heaven ought to be handled with utmost impartiality; when something is good, one should follow it.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Affairs of state should be handled with complete impartiality; when a proposal is sound, one should accept it.

sentences.zh: 德彝所言，真得大體，臣誠心服，不敢遂非。」

translations.literal: What Deyi said truly grasps the larger principle; your servant sincerely submits in heart and dares not persist in error."
translations.idiomatic: What Feng Deyi said truly grasps the larger principle. I am sincerely convinced and dare not persist in my error."

sentences.zh: 上悅曰：「公等各能如是，朕復何憂！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "If you gentlemen can all be like this, what further worry have I!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure: "If you gentlemen can all act this way, what have I to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 右驍衛大將軍長孫順德受人饋絹，事覺，上曰：「順德果能有益國家，朕與之共有府庫耳，何至貪冒如是乎！」

translations.literal: Zhangsun Shunde, great general of the Right Courageous Cavalry Guard, accepted a gift of silk from someone. When the matter came to light, the Emperor said: "If Shunde can truly benefit the state, I would share the treasury with him—how could he be so greedy and corrupt!
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shunde, great general of the Right Courageous Cavalry Guard, accepted a gift of silk. When the matter came to light, the emperor said: "If Shunde can truly serve the state well, I would share the treasury with him—how could he be so greedy!

sentences.zh: 猶惜其有功，不之罪，但於殿庭賜絹數十匹。

translations.literal: Still cherishing his past merit, he did not punish him, but only bestowed on him several dozen bolts of silk in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Still valuing his past service, the emperor did not punish him but instead gave him several dozen bolts of silk in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿胡演曰：「順德枉法受財，罪不可赦，奈何復賜之絹？」

translations.literal: Hu Yan, vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, said: "Shunde perverted the law and accepted wealth; the crime cannot be pardoned—why bestow silk on him again?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yan, vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, said: "Shunde perverted the law and accepted a bribe; his crime cannot be pardoned—why reward him with more silk?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「彼有人性，得絹之辱，甚於受刑；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "He has human feelings; to receive silk as a humiliation is worse than receiving punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "He has human feelings; the humiliation of receiving silk as a reward is worse than formal punishment;

sentences.zh: 如不知愧，一禽獸耳，殺之何益！」

translations.literal: if he knows no shame, he is merely a beast—what use in killing him!"
translations.idiomatic: if he feels no shame, he is no better than a beast, and killing him would serve no purpose!"

sentences.zh: 辛丑，天節將軍燕郡王李藝據涇州反。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Li Yi, general of Heavenly Integrity and Prince of Yan Commandery, seized Jing Prefecture and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Li Yi, general of Heavenly Integrity and Prince of Yan Commandery, seized Jing Prefecture and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 藝之初入朝也，恃功驕倨，秦王左右至其營，藝無故毆之。

translations.literal: When Yi first entered the capital for audience, relying on his merit he was arrogant and insolent; when attendants of the Prince of Qin came to his camp, Yi beat them for no cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yi first came to court, he was arrogant and overbearing on account of his merit; when attendants of the Prince of Qin came to his camp, he beat them without cause.

sentences.zh: 上皇怒，收藝繫獄，既而釋之。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was angry, seized Yi, and imprisoned him, but afterward released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor was enraged, had Yi arrested and imprisoned, but later released him.

sentences.zh: 上即位，藝內不自安。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, Yi inwardly could not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Li Yi grew uneasy within.

sentences.zh: 曹州妖巫李五戒謂藝曰：「王貴色已發！」

translations.literal: Li Wujie, a sorcerer of Caozhou, said to Yi: "Your noble aura has already appeared!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Wujie, a sorcerer of Caozhou, told Li Yi: "Your noble aura has already appeared!"

sentences.zh: 勸之反。

translations.literal: He urged him to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Li Yi to rebel.

sentences.zh: 藝乃詐稱奉密敕，勒兵入朝。

translations.literal: Yi then falsely claimed he was acting on a secret edict and mustered troops to enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi then falsely claimed to be acting on a secret edict and mustered his troops to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵至幽州，幽州治中趙慈皓馳出謁之，藝入據幽州。

translations.literal: He then led his troops to You Prefecture. Zhao Cihao, acting prefect of You Prefecture, galloped out to meet him, and Yi entered and seized You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched on You Prefecture. Zhao Cihao, acting prefect of You Prefecture, rode out to meet him, and Li Yi entered and seized the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部尚書長孫無忌等為行軍總管以討之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhangsun Wuji, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and others as campaign commanders to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhangsun Wuji, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and others as campaign commanders to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 趙慈皓聞官軍將至，密與統軍楊岌圖之，事洩，藝囚慈皓。

translations.literal: Zhao Cihao, hearing that the imperial army was about to arrive, secretly plotted with Yang Ji, commander of the garrison, but the affair leaked out and Yi imprisoned Cihao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Cihao heard that the imperial army was approaching, he secretly plotted with Yang Ji, commander of the garrison, but the plot was discovered and Li Yi imprisoned Zhao.

sentences.zh: 岌在城外覺變，勒兵攻之，藝眾潰，棄妻子，將奔突厥。

translations.literal: Ji, outside the city, perceived the change, mustered troops and attacked; Yi's forces collapsed, and he abandoned his wife and children, intending to flee to the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, outside the city, realized what had happened, mustered troops, and attacked. Li Yi's forces collapsed; he abandoned his wife and children and fled toward the Türks.

sentences.zh: 至烏氏，左右斬之，傳首長安。

translations.literal: When he reached Wushi, his attendants beheaded him and sent his head to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At Wushi, his attendants beheaded him and sent his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 弟壽，為利州都督，亦坐誅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shou, who was military governor of Lizhou, was also executed on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shou, military governor of Lizhou, was also executed in connection with the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 初，隋末喪亂，豪傑並起，擁眾據地，自相雄長；

translations.literal: Earlier, amid the ruin and disorder at the end of Sui, heroes rose together, gathering followers and seizing territory, each making himself a local strongman;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, amid the chaos at the end of the Sui, local strongmen rose everywhere, gathering followers, seizing territory, and ruling as rival chieftains;

sentences.zh: 唐興，相帥來歸，上皇為之割置州縣以寵祿之，由是州縣之數，倍於開皇、大業之間。

translations.literal: when Tang arose, they came in succession to submit; the Retired Emperor carved out and established prefectures and counties to honor and reward them, and thereby the number of prefectures and counties doubled what it had been between the Kaihuang and Daye reigns.
translations.idiomatic: when the Tang rose, they submitted in succession, and the Retired Emperor carved out new prefectures and counties to honor and reward them. As a result, the number of prefectures and counties doubled what it had been under the Kaihuang and Daye reigns.

sentences.zh: 上以民少吏多，思革其弊；

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the people were few and officials many, wished to reform this abuse;
translations.idiomatic: Because the people were too few and officials too many, the emperor sought to reform the abuse;

sentences.zh: 二月，命大加並省，因山川形便，分為十道：一曰關內，二曰河南，三曰河東，四曰河北，五曰山南，六曰隴右，七曰淮南，八曰江南，九曰劍南，十曰嶺南。

translations.literal: in the second month he ordered a great consolidation and reduction of offices; following the convenience of mountains and rivers, the realm was divided into ten circuits: first, Guannei; second, Henan; third, Hedong; fourth, Hebei; fifth, Shannan; sixth, Longyou; seventh, Huainan; eighth, Jiangnan; ninth, Jiannan; tenth, Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month he ordered a major consolidation of administrative units. Following natural geography, the realm was divided into ten circuits: Guannei, Henan, Hedong, Hebei, Shannan, Longyou, Huainan, Jiangnan, Jiannan, and Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸巳，皇后帥內外命婦親蠶。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guisi, the empress led the inner and outer titled ladies in personally tending the silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guisi, the empress led the palace ladies and other titled women in the ceremonial tending of silkworms.

sentences.zh: 閏月，癸丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day guichou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guichou, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上謂太子少師蕭瑀曰：「朕少好弓矢，得良弓十數，自謂無以加，近以示弓工，乃曰『皆非良材』。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Emperor said to Xiao Yu, junior preceptor to the crown prince: "In my youth I loved bows and arrows and obtained more than ten fine bows; I thought none could surpass them. Recently I showed them to a bow-maker, and he said, 'None are made of good wood.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the emperor said to Xiao Yu, junior preceptor to the crown prince: "In my youth I loved bows and arrows and acquired more than ten fine bows; I thought nothing could surpass them. Recently I showed them to a bow-maker, who said, 'None of these are made of good wood.

sentences.zh: 朕問其故，工曰：『木心不直，則脈理皆邪，弓雖勁而發矢不直。』

translations.literal: I asked the reason, and the craftsman said: 'If the heart of the wood is not straight, then the grain is all awry; though the bow may be strong, the arrow it shoots will not fly straight.'
translations.idiomatic: I asked why, and the craftsman said: 'If the heart of the wood is not straight, the grain runs awry; though the bow may be strong, the arrow it shoots will not fly true.'

sentences.zh: 朕始寤向者辨之未精也。

translations.literal: I then first understood that my earlier judgment had not been precise.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did I realize that my earlier judgment had not been precise.

sentences.zh: 朕以弓矢定四方，識之猶未能盡，況天下之務，其能遍知乎！」

translations.literal: I took the four quarters with bow and arrow, yet my knowledge of them is still not complete—how much less can I know comprehensively the affairs of all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: I conquered the realm with bow and arrow, yet I still do not fully understand even that—how then can I hope to know everything about governing the empire!"

sentences.zh: 乃命京官五品以上更宿中書內省，數延見，問以民間疾苦，政事得失。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered capital officials of the fifth rank and above to take turns lodging overnight in the Secretariat and Inner Chancery; he repeatedly summoned them for audience and questioned them about the people's hardships and the gains and losses of government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered capital officials of the fifth rank and above to take turns lodging at the Secretariat and Inner Chancery, summoning them repeatedly to inquire about popular hardship and the successes and failures of government policy.

sentences.zh: 涼州都督長樂王幼良，性粗暴，左右百餘人，皆無賴子弟，侵暴百姓；

translations.literal: Youliang, Prince of Changle and military governor of Liang Prefecture, was by nature rough and violent; more than a hundred of his attendants were all worthless young men who oppressed and plundered the common people;
translations.idiomatic: Youliang, Prince of Changle and military governor of Liang Prefecture, was violent by nature; his more than one hundred attendants were all worthless young toughs who abused the populace;

sentences.zh: 又與羌、胡互市。

translations.literal: He also traded with the Qiang and the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He also engaged in border trade with the Qiang and other non-Han peoples.

sentences.zh: 或告幼良有異志，上遣中書令宇文士及馳驛代之，並按其事。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Youliang harbored disloyal ambitions; the Emperor sent Chief Director of the Secretariat Yuwen Shiji by post-horse relay to replace him and also to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Youliang harbored treasonous ambitions, Emperor Taizong sent Chief Director of the Secretariat Yuwen Shiji by fast courier to replace him and investigate the charges.

sentences.zh: 左右懼，謀劫幼良入北虜，又欲殺士及據有河西。

translations.literal: His attendants were afraid; they plotted to abduct Youliang into the northern barbarians, and also intended to kill Shiji and seize control of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants grew fearful and plotted to seize Youliang and flee to the northern barbarians, while also planning to kill Shiji and take control of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 復有告其謀者，夏，四月，癸巳，賜幼良死。

translations.literal: Again someone reported their plot; in summer, the fourth month, on guisi, Youliang was granted death by imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: When someone again reported the plot, in summer, the fourth month, on guisi, the emperor ordered Youliang to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 五月，苑君璋帥眾來降。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Yuan Junzhang led his forces and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Yuan Junzhang arrived with his followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 初，君璋引突厥陷馬邑，殺高滿政，退保恆安。

translations.literal: Initially, Junzhang brought in the Türks to capture Mayi, killed Gao Manzheng, and retreated to hold Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Junzhang had led the Türks in the capture of Mayi, killed Gao Manzheng, and then withdrew to defend Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 其眾皆中國人，多棄君璋來降。

translations.literal: His troops were all Chinese; many abandoned Junzhang and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were all Chinese, and many deserted him to surrender to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 君璋懼，亦降，請捍北邊以贖罪，上皇許之。

translations.literal: Junzhang was afraid and also surrendered, requesting to defend the northern border to redeem his guilt; the Retired Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his safety, Yuan Junzhang also surrendered and asked to guard the northern frontier in atonement for his crimes; the Retired Emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 君璋請約契，上皇雁門人元普賜之金券。

translations.literal: Junzhang requested a covenant; the Retired Emperor had Yuan Pu of Yanmen present him with a gold bond.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang asked for a formal covenant, and the Retired Emperor had Yuan Pu of Yanmen bestow on him a written pledge backed by gold.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗復遣人招之，君璋猶豫未決，恆安人郭子威說君璋以「恆安地險城堅，突厥方強，且當倚之以觀變，未可束手於人。」

translations.literal: Qaghan Jieli again sent men to win him over; Junzhang wavered and could not decide. Guo Ziwei of Heng'an said to Junzhang: "Heng'an has treacherous terrain and stout walls; the Türks are now strong—we should rely on this position to watch how events unfold and must not submit helplessly to others."
translations.idiomatic: When Qaghan Jieli again sent emissaries to win him back, Yuan Junzhang hesitated. Guo Ziwei of Heng'an urged him: "Heng'an lies in rugged terrain behind strong walls, and the Türks are still powerful—you should hold the place and watch how matters turn before yielding yourself into someone else's hands."

sentences.zh: 君璋乃執元普送突厥，復與之合，數與突厥入寇。

translations.literal: Junzhang thereupon seized Yuan Pu and sent him to the Türks, again joined them, and repeatedly raided together with the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang then seized Yuan Pu and handed him over to the Türks, resumed his alliance with them, and repeatedly joined them in raids across the border.

sentences.zh: 至是，見頡利政亂，知其不足恃，遂帥眾來降。

translations.literal: At this time, seeing Jieli's government in disorder, knowing he could not be relied upon, he therefore led his forces and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Now, seeing that Jieli's rule had fallen into chaos and that he could no longer be counted on, Yuan Junzhang came to surrender with his followers.

sentences.zh: 上以君璋為隰州都督、芮國公。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Junzhang military governor of Xi Prefecture and Duke of the State of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong appointed him military governor of Xi Prefecture and enfeoffed him as Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 有上書請去佞臣者，上問：「佞臣為誰？」

translations.literal: Someone submitted a memorial requesting the removal of flatterers; the Emperor asked: "Who are the flatterers?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone submitted a memorial asking that sycophants be removed from court, Emperor Taizong asked: "Who are the sycophants?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣居草澤，不能的知其人，願陛下與群臣言，或陽怒以試之，彼執理不屈者，直臣也，畏威順旨者，佞臣也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant lives in the wilds and cannot identify the men with certainty. I wish Your Majesty would speak with the ministers—perhaps feign anger to test them: those who hold to principle and do not yield are upright ministers; those who fear authority and comply with your wishes are flatterers."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I am a private subject and cannot name them with certainty. Your Majesty might speak with your ministers and perhaps feign anger to test them: those who stand firm on principle are upright officials; those who fear your wrath and simply agree are flatterers."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「君，源也；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The ruler is the source;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "The ruler is the source;

sentences.zh: 臣，流也；

translations.literal: ministers are the stream;
translations.idiomatic: the ministers are the stream;

sentences.zh: 濁其源而求其流之清，不可得矣。

translations.literal: To muddy the source yet seek clearness in the stream—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If you muddy the source and then expect the stream to run clear, you will never succeed.

sentences.zh: 君自為詐，何以責臣下之直乎！

translations.literal: If the ruler himself practices deception, how can he demand uprightness from his subordinates!
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign himself resorts to deception, how can he demand honesty from those beneath him!

sentences.zh: 朕方以至誠治天下，見前世帝王好以權譎小數接其臣下者，常竊恥之。

translations.literal: I am now governing all under Heaven with utmost sincerity; when I see former emperors who liked to use schemes and petty tricks in dealing with their ministers, I have always privately felt ashamed of this.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to govern the empire with complete sincerity. I have always felt ashamed when I see how past emperors tested their ministers with trickery and petty stratagems.

sentences.zh: 卿策雖善，朕不取也。」

translations.literal: Your plan, though good, I will not adopt."
translations.idiomatic: Your plan may be clever, but I will not adopt it."

sentences.zh: 六月，辛巳，右僕射密明公封德彝薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinsi, Feng Deyi, Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and Secret Duke of Mimeng, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi, Feng Deyi, Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Mimeng, died.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，復以太子少師蕭瑀為左僕射。

translations.literal: On renchen, Xiao Yu, junior preceptor to the crown prince, was again appointed Left Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Xiao Yu, junior preceptor to the crown prince, was again appointed Left Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 戊申，上與侍臣論周、秦修短，蕭瑀對曰：「紂為不道，武王征之。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Emperor discussed with his attending ministers the long and short reigns of Zhou and Qin; Xiao Yu replied: "King Zhou was without the Way, and King Wu attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Emperor Taizong discussed with his attending ministers why the Zhou and Qin dynasties endured or perished so differently. Xiao Yu replied: "King Zhou of Shang was tyrannical, and King Wu of Zhou campaigned against him.

sentences.zh: 周及六國無罪，始皇滅之。

translations.literal: Zhou and the six states were without guilt, yet the First Emperor destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: The states of Zhou and the six kingdoms were guiltless, yet the First Emperor destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 得天下雖同，人心則異。」

translations.literal: Gaining the realm was the same in both cases, but the people's hearts differed."
translations.idiomatic: Both conquered the realm, yet the people's hearts were not the same."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公知其一，未知其二。
