translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You know the first point but not the second.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "You understand one part of this, but not the whole of it.

sentences.zh: 周得天下，增修仁義；

translations.literal: Zhou gained the realm and further cultivated benevolence and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou gained the realm, they cultivated benevolence and righteousness all the more;

sentences.zh: 秦得天下，益尚詐力；

translations.literal: Qin gained the realm and further esteemed deception and force;
translations.idiomatic: after Qin gained the realm, it relied ever more on deceit and brute force;

sentences.zh: 此修短之所以殊也。

translations.literal: This is why their durations were different.
translations.idiomatic: that is why one endured and the other perished so quickly.

sentences.zh: 蓋取之或可以逆得，守之不可以不順故也。」

translations.literal: Presumably what is taken may sometimes be gained by irregular means, but what is held cannot fail to accord with the Way."
translations.idiomatic: A throne may sometimes be won by irregular means, but it cannot be held except by governing in accord with the Way."

sentences.zh: 瑀謝不及。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu apologized that he had not reached so far.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu apologized for his inadequacy.

sentences.zh: 山東大旱，詔所在賑恤，無出今年租賦。

translations.literal: A great drought struck east of the mountains; an edict ordered relief and succor wherever needed, with no collection of this year's land tax and levies.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought struck the eastern provinces. An edict ordered local officials to provide famine relief and waived this year's taxes and levies.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬子，以吏部尚書長孫無忌為右僕射。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renzi, Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed Right Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renzi, Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Right Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 無忌與上為布衣交，加以外戚，有佐命功，上委以腹心，其禮遇群臣莫及，欲用為宰相者數矣。

translations.literal: Wuji and the Emperor had been friends when both were commoners; added to this was his status as a maternal relative and his merit in aiding the founding of the dynasty—the Emperor entrusted him as a confidant, and no minister received treatment to compare; several times he had wished to appoint him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji had been Emperor Taizong's friend since their days as private citizens; as the emperor's maternal relative, he had also earned merit in establishing the dynasty. The emperor trusted him as a close confidant and treated no other minister with such favor, and had wanted several times to appoint him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后固請曰：「妾備位椒房，家之貴寵極矣，誠不願兄弟復執國政。

translations.literal: Empress Wende firmly pleaded: "Your servant occupies the position in the inner palace; my family's honor and favor have already reached the utmost—I truly do not wish my brothers again to hold national power.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende strongly urged him: "I already occupy the empress's place, and my family's honor and favor have reached their limit. I truly do not wish my brothers to hold state power again.

sentences.zh: 呂、霍、上官，可為切骨之戒，幸陛下矜察！」

translations.literal: The Lü, Huo, and Shangguan families may serve as warnings burned into the bone—may Your Majesty kindly examine this!"
translations.idiomatic: The examples of the Lü, Huo, and Shangguan clans should be a warning carved into the bone. I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully!"

sentences.zh: 上不聽，卒用之。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen and in the end appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong would not heed her and ultimately appointed him.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥性淳厚，政令質略。

translations.literal: Initially, the Türks were simple and honest in character, and their government orders were plain and uncomplicated.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Türks were a plain and honest people, and their government was simple and unadorned.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗得華人趙德言，委用之。

translations.literal: Qaghan Jieli obtained the Chinese Zhao Deyan and entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qaghan Jieli gained the services of the Chinese advisor Zhao Deyan, he put him in charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 德言專其威福，多變更舊俗，政令煩苛，國人始不悅。

translations.literal: Deyan monopolized authority and favor, changed many old customs, and made government orders burdensome and harsh—the people of the state at first grew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deyan monopolized power and privilege, changed many old Türk customs, and imposed burdensome regulations, and the Türk people soon grew dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 頡利又好信任諸胡而疏突厥，胡人貪冒，多反覆，兵革歲動；

translations.literal: Jieli also liked to trust the various Hu peoples and keep his distance from the Türks; the Hu were greedy and corrupt, often turned traitor, and weapons of war moved every year;
translations.idiomatic: Jieli also preferred to trust the various Hu peoples while distancing himself from the Türks; the Hu were greedy and unreliable, frequently switching sides, and war continued year after year;

sentences.zh: 會大雪，深數尺，雜畜多死，連年饑饉，民皆凍餒。

translations.literal: There came heavy snow several feet deep; mixed livestock mostly died; famine continued for years, and the people all suffered cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Then heavy snow fell several feet deep, many livestock perished, famine continued for years, and the people suffered from cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 頡利用度不給，重斂諸部，由是內外離怨，諸部多叛，兵浸弱。

translations.literal: Jieli's expenditures were insufficient; he heavily levied the various tribes—thereby inner and outer turned alienated and resentful, many tribes rebelled, and his military strength gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli's resources ran short, and he imposed heavy taxes on the tribes. Internal and external resentment followed, many tribes rebelled, and his military strength gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 言事者多請擊之，上以問蕭瑀、長孫無忌曰：「頡利君臣昏虐，危亡可必。

translations.literal: Many who spoke on policy requested an attack; the Emperor asked Xiao Yu and Zhangsun Wuji: "Jieli's ruler and ministers are benighted and tyrannical—fall and ruin are certain.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials urged an attack on the Türks. Emperor Taizong asked Xiao Yu and Zhangsun Wuji: "Jieli and his ministers are corrupt and cruel; their collapse is certain.

sentences.zh: 今擊之，則新與之盟；

translations.literal: If we attack now, it would break the alliance just made with them;
translations.idiomatic: If we attack now, we break the alliance we have only just concluded with them;

sentences.zh: 不擊，恐失機會；

translations.literal: If we do not attack, I fear we may lose the opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: if we do not attack, I fear we may miss our opportunity;

sentences.zh: 如何而可？」

translations.literal: What will do?"
translations.idiomatic: What should we do?"

sentences.zh: 瑀請擊之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu requested to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu urged an attack.

sentences.zh: 無忌對曰：「虜不犯塞而棄信勞民，非王者之師也。」

translations.literal: Wuji replied: "When the barbarians have not violated the border passes yet we abandon faith and wear out the people—this is not the army of a true king."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji replied: "If they have not violated the frontier yet we break faith and exhaust our people on campaign, that is not the conduct of a true sovereign's army."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 上問公卿以享國久長之策，蕭瑀言：「三代封建而久長，秦孤立而速亡。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the nobles and ministers about policies for long enduring possession of the state; Xiao Yu said: "The Three Dynasties practiced enfeoffment and endured long; Qin stood alone and perished swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong asked his ministers how to secure the long endurance of the dynasty. Xiao Yu said: "The Three Dynasties enfeoffed feudal lords and endured for ages; Qin ruled alone and fell quickly."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，於是始有封建之議。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered this correct, and from this there first arose discussion of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong agreed, and from that point the court began debating enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎王珪有密奏，附侍中高士廉，寢而不言。

translations.literal: Wang Gui, vice director of the Yellow Gate, had a secret memorial; it was handed to Gao Shilian, attendant grandee, who kept it and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, vice director of the Yellow Gate, submitted a confidential memorial, but handed it to Attendant Grandee Gao Shilian, who shelved it and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，八月，戊戌，出士廉為安州大都督。

translations.literal: When the Emperor learned of this, in the eighth month, on wuxu, he demoted Shilian to be grand commander of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong learned of this, in the eighth month, on wuxu, he transferred Gao Shilian to serve as grand commander of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day gengxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengxu, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，中書令宇文士及罷為殿中監，御史大夫杜淹參豫朝政。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Yuwen Shiji, Chief Director of the Secretariat, was removed and made director of the Palace Domestic Service; Du Yan, chief imperial censor, participated in deliberating on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Yuwen Shiji was dismissed as Chief Director of the Secretariat and appointed director of the Palace Domestic Service, while Du Yan, chief imperial censor, was brought in to participate in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 他官參豫政事自此始。

translations.literal: From this began the participation of other officials in deliberating on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the beginning of officials outside the inner secretariat participating in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 淹薦刑部員外郎邸懷道，上問其行能，對曰：「煬帝將幸江都，召百官問行留之計，懷道為吏部主事，獨言不可。

translations.literal: Du Yan recommended Di Huaidao, an assistant director in the Ministry of Justice; the Emperor asked about his conduct and ability, and he replied: "When Emperor Yang was about to proceed to Jiangdu, he summoned the hundred officials to ask whether to go or stay; Huaidao was a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and alone said it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan recommended Di Huaidao, an assistant director in the Ministry of Justice. When Emperor Taizong asked about his character and ability, Du Yan replied: "When Emperor Yang was about to travel south to Jiangdu, he summoned the officials to ask whether he should go or stay. Huaidao was then a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and he alone said the journey should not be made.

sentences.zh: 臣親見之。」

translations.literal: Your servant saw it with his own eyes."
translations.idiomatic: I saw this with my own eyes."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿稱懷道為是，何為自不正諫？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You say Huaidao was right—why then did you yourself not offer straight remonstrance?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "You say Huaidao was right—then why did you not remonstrate yourself?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣爾日不居重任，又知諫不從，徒死無益。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant at that time did not hold an important post, and I also knew that remonstrance would not be heeded—to die for nothing would be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "At the time I did not hold an important post, and I knew remonstrance would not be heeded—dying for nothing would have served no purpose."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿知煬帝不可諫，何為立其朝？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You knew Emperor Yang could not be remonstrated with—why then did you take office in his court?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "If you knew Emperor Yang would not listen, why did you serve in his court at all?

sentences.zh: 既立其朝，何得不諫？

translations.literal: Once you took office in his court, how could you fail to remonstrate?
translations.idiomatic: Once you accepted office in his court, how could you not remonstrate?

sentences.zh: 卿仕隋，容可雲位卑；

translations.literal: You served Sui—one might say your position was low;
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui court one might say your rank was too low;

sentences.zh: 後仕王世充，尊顯矣，何得亦不諫？」

translations.literal: Later you served Wang Shichong, when you were honored and eminent—how could you also fail to remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: but later you served Wang Shichong in a prominent position—why did you still not remonstrate then?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣於世充非不諫，但不從耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant with Shichong was not without remonstrance—it was only that he would not listen."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "With Wang Shichong I did remonstrate; he simply would not listen."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「世充若賢而納諫，不應亡國；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If Shichong were worthy and accepted remonstrance, he ought not to have lost the state;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "If Wang Shichong had been virtuous and heeded remonstrance, his state would not have fallen;

sentences.zh: 若暴而拒諫，卿何得免禍？」

translations.literal: If he were violent and rejected remonstrance, how could you have escaped calamity?"
translations.idiomatic: if he was tyrannical and refused advice, how did you escape punishment?"

sentences.zh: 淹不能對。

translations.literal: Du Yan could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan had no answer.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「今日可謂尊任矣，可以諫未？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Today you may be said to hold honored trust—can you now remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "Today you hold high trust—will you remonstrate now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「願盡死。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I wish to give my life entirely."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I will give my life if need be."

sentences.zh: 上笑。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed.

sentences.zh: 辛未，幽州都督王君廓謀叛，道死。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Wang Jun'guo, military governor of You Prefecture, plotted rebellion and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Wang Jun'guo, military governor of You Prefecture, plotted rebellion but died on the road before carrying it out.

sentences.zh: 君廓在州，驕縱多不法，征入朝。

translations.literal: Jun'guo, while in the prefecture, was proud and unrestrained and committed many unlawful acts; he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in You Prefecture, Wang Jun'guo had grown arrogant and lawless, and was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 長史李玄道，房玄齡從甥也，憑君廓附書，君廓私發之，不識草書，疑其告己罪，行至渭南，殺驛吏而逃；

translations.literal: Chief secretary Li Xuandao, a nephew of Fang Xuanling on his mother's side, entrusted Jun'guo with a letter to deliver; Jun'guo opened it privately, could not read cursive script, suspected it reported his crimes, and when he reached Weinan killed the post-station clerk and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Li Xuandao, a nephew of Fang Xuanling on his mother's side, asked Wang Jun'guo to deliver a letter for him. Jun'guo opened it secretly, could not read cursive script, suspected it denounced his crimes, and when he reached Weinan he killed a post-station clerk and fled;

sentences.zh: 將奔突厥，為野人所殺。

translations.literal: He was about to flee to the Türks but was killed by country folk.
translations.idiomatic: He was fleeing toward the Türks when he was killed by local hunters.

sentences.zh: 嶺南酋長馮盎、談殿等迭相攻擊，久未入朝，諸州奏稱盎反，前後以十數；

translations.literal: The chieftains of Lingnan, Feng Ang, Tan Dian, and others, attacked one another in turn; for a long time they had not entered court; various prefectures memorialized that Ang had rebelled, more than ten such reports in all;
translations.idiomatic: In Lingnan, chieftains such as Feng Ang and Tan Dian attacked one another in turn and had long failed to come to court. Prefectures submitted report after report—more than ten in all—that Feng Ang had rebelled;

sentences.zh: 上命將軍藺謨等發江、嶺數十州兵討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered General Lan Mo and others to mobilize troops from several tens of prefectures along the Yangzi and in Lingnan to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered General Lan Mo and others to mobilize troops from dozens of prefectures along the Yangzi and in Lingnan to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「中國初定，嶺南瘴癘險遠，不可以宿大兵。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "China has only just been settled; Lingnan has malarial pestilence and is dangerous and remote—it is not a place to station a large army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "The empire has only just been pacified. Lingnan is distant, malarial, and treacherous; it is no place for a large army.

sentences.zh: 且盎反狀未成，未宜動眾。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the signs of Ang's rebellion are not yet established—it is not yet fitting to move the masses."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Feng Ang's rebellion has not yet been clearly established. It is too soon to mobilize on such a scale."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「告者道路不絕，何雲反狀未成？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Informants have not ceased along the roads—how can you say the signs of rebellion are not established?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "Reports keep arriving without pause—how can you say the rebellion is not yet established?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「盎若反，必分兵據險，攻掠州縣。

translations.literal: He replied: "If Ang had rebelled, he would surely divide his forces to hold strategic passes and attack and plunder prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng answered: "If Feng Ang had truly rebelled, he would have divided his forces to hold the mountain passes and raided the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 今告者已數年，而兵不出境，此不反明矣。

translations.literal: Now reports have continued for several years, yet his troops have not crossed the border—this clearly shows he has not rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Reports have been coming for years, yet his forces have never crossed the border. That is clear proof he has not rebelled.

sentences.zh: 諸州既疑其反，陛下又不遣使鎮撫，彼畏死，故不敢入朝。

translations.literal: Since the prefectures already suspect him of rebellion, and Your Majesty also has not sent emissaries to reassure and soothe them, they fear death and therefore dare not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures already suspect him of rebellion, and Your Majesty has sent no envoy to reassure him. Fearing for their lives, they dare not come to court.

sentences.zh: 若遣信臣示以至誠，彼喜於免禍，可不煩兵而服。」

translations.literal: If you send a trusted minister to show utmost sincerity, they will rejoice at escaping calamity, and submission may be gained without troubling the army."
translations.idiomatic: If you send a trusted envoy in good faith, they will rejoice at escaping disaster, and you can win their submission without sending troops."

sentences.zh: 上乃罷兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon dismissed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor canceled the campaign.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙酉，遣員外散騎侍郎李公掩持節慰諭之，盎遣其子智戴隨使者入朝。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, he sent Li Gongyan, vice director of the Scattered Cavalry, bearing credentials to console and instruct them; Ang sent his son Zhizai to follow the envoy into court.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, he dispatched Li Gongyan, vice director of the Scattered Cavalry, with imperial credentials to offer reassurance. Feng Ang sent his son Zhizai to accompany the envoy to court.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「魏徵令我發一介之使，而嶺表遂安，勝十萬之師，不可不賞。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Wei Zheng had me send a single envoy, and the region south of the Ling Range was thereby pacified—better than an army of a hundred thousand; this cannot go unrewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "Wei Zheng persuaded me to send a single envoy, and the Lingnan region was pacified at once—that outdid an army of a hundred thousand men. Such service must be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 賜征絹五百匹。

translations.literal: He granted Wei Zheng five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Wei Zheng with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬午，左僕射蕭瑀坐事免。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renwu, Xiao Yu, Left Director of the Department of State Affairs, was removed from office on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renwu, Xiao Yu, Left Director of the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 戊申，利州都督義安王李孝常等謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: On wushen, Li Xiaochang, Prince of Yi'an and military governor of Li Prefecture, and others plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Li Xiaochang, Prince of Yi'an and military governor of Li Prefecture, and his co-conspirators plotted rebellion and were executed.

sentences.zh: 孝常因入朝，留京師，與右武衛將軍劉德裕及其甥統軍元弘善、監門將軍長孫安業互說符命，謀以宿衛兵作亂。

translations.literal: Xiaochang, having come for court audience, remained in the capital; with Liu Deyu, general of the Right Martial Guard, and his nephew Yuan Hongshan, commander of troops, and Zhangsun Anye, general of the Gate Guard, he spoke to one another of portents and destinies, plotting to use the palace guard troops to raise a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaochang had come to court and remained in the capital. Together with Liu Deyu, general of the Right Martial Guard, his nephew Yuan Hongshan, a troop commander, and Zhangsun Anye, general of the Gate Guard, he traded talk of portents and destiny, plotting to raise a rebellion with the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 安業，皇后之異母兄也，嗜酒無賴；

translations.literal: Anye was the empress's half-brother on her father's side; he was addicted to wine and worthless;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Anye was the empress's elder half-brother by a different mother; he was a drunkard and a ne'er-do-well;

sentences.zh: 父晟卒，弟無忌及後並幼，安業斥還舅氏。

translations.literal: When their father Sheng died, the younger brother Wuji and the empress were both still young, and Anye was sent back to his mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: After their father Zhangsun Sheng died, Wuji and the empress were both still young, and Anye was sent back to live with his mother's clan.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，後不以舊怨為意，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, the empress did not harbor old resentments and treated him with great favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, the empress set aside old grievances and treated him with great generosity and honor.

sentences.zh: 及反事覺，後涕泣為之固請曰：「安業罪誠當萬死。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was discovered, the empress wept and pleaded insistently on his behalf, saying: "An Ye's crime truly deserves death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was uncovered, the empress wept and pleaded earnestly for him: "An Ye's crime truly merits death.

sentences.zh: 然不慈於妾，天下知之；

translations.literal: Yet his lack of kindness toward me is known throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his unkindness toward me is known throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 今置以極刑，人必謂妾所為，恐亦為聖朝之累。」

translations.literal: If he is now punished with the extreme penalty, people will surely say I arranged it, and I fear it will also bring disgrace upon the sacred dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: If he is now executed, people will surely believe I engineered it, and I fear it would bring shame upon the dynasty as well."

sentences.zh: 由是得減死，流巂州。

translations.literal: Because of this he received a reduced sentence from death and was banished to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On this account his sentence was reduced from death, and he was exiled to Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或告右丞魏徵私其親戚，上使御史大夫溫彥博按之，無狀。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Vice Director Wei Zheng had favored his relatives in private matters. Emperor Taizong sent Grand Censor Wen Yanbo to investigate; no evidence was found.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Vice Director Wei Zheng of showing private favor to his kinsmen. Emperor Taizong sent Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo to investigate, but no wrongdoing was found.

sentences.zh: 彥博言於上曰：「征不存形跡，遠避嫌疑，心雖無私，亦有可責。」

translations.literal: Yanbo said to the emperor: "Zheng does not guard his outward conduct or keep far from suspicion; though his heart is without private intent, he is still open to censure."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo told Emperor Taizong: "Zheng does not watch his conduct or keep clear of suspicion; though his intentions are honest, he is still blameworthy."

sentences.zh: 上令彥博讓征，且曰：「自今宜存形跡。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yanbo to reprove Zheng, and also said: "From now on you ought to guard your outward conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had Yanbo rebuke Zheng, adding: "From now on you should mind your conduct."

sentences.zh: 它日，征入見，言於上曰：「臣聞君臣同體，宜相與盡誠；

translations.literal: On another day, Zheng entered to see the emperor and said: "Your subject has heard that ruler and minister are one body and ought to be utterly sincere with each other;
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Zheng came before the emperor and said: "I have heard that sovereign and minister share one body and should treat each other with complete sincerity;

sentences.zh: 若上下但存形跡，則國之興喪尚未可知，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: If above and below attend only to outward appearances, then whether the state will rise or fall cannot yet be known—I dare not obey such an edict."
translations.idiomatic: If ruler and minister care only for appearances, then whether the realm will prosper or perish cannot be foretold—I dare not accept such an order."

sentences.zh: 上瞿然曰：「吾已悔之。」

translations.literal: The emperor, startled, said: "I already regret it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong started and said: "I already regret saying that."

sentences.zh: 征再拜曰：「臣幸得奉事陛下，願使臣為良臣，勿為忠臣。」

translations.literal: Zheng bowed twice and said: "Your subject is fortunate to serve Your Majesty; I wish you would make me a good minister and not a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng bowed again and said: "I am fortunate to serve Your Majesty; I pray you will make me a good minister rather than a loyal one."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「忠、良有以異乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Are 'loyal' and 'good' any different?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong asked: "Is there any difference between 'loyal' and 'good'?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「稷、契、皋陶，君臣協心，俱享尊榮，所謂良臣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Hou Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao—ruler and ministers worked in accord and all enjoyed honor and glory; these are what are called good ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Hou Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao—sovereign and ministers worked in harmony and all shared honor and glory; these are what we call good ministers.

sentences.zh: 龍逄、比干，面折廷爭，身誅國亡，所謂忠臣。」

translations.literal: Long Feng and Bi Gan confronted the ruler directly and disputed in court; their persons were executed and their states perished; these are what are called loyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Long Feng and Bi Gan confronted their rulers face to face and fought them in open court; they were put to death and their states were destroyed—these are what we call loyal ministers."

sentences.zh: 上悅，賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and granted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was delighted and awarded him five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 上神采英毅，群臣進見者，皆失舉措；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong's bearing was spirited and stern; all ministers who came forward to audience lost their composure;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong's presence was sharp and commanding; ministers who came to audience often lost their composure;

sentences.zh: 上知之，每見人奏事，必假以辭色，冀聞規諫。

translations.literal: Knowing this, whenever he received someone presenting business, he always assumed a gentle expression in the hope of hearing remonstrance and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Aware of this, whenever someone came to report business, he would deliberately soften his manner, hoping to draw out frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂公卿曰：「人欲自見其形，必資明鏡；

translations.literal: He once told the high officials: "If a man wishes to see his own form, he must rely on a bright mirror;
translations.idiomatic: He once told the chief ministers: "If a man wishes to see his own face, he needs a bright mirror;

sentences.zh: 君欲自知其過，必待忠臣。

translations.literal: If a ruler wishes to know his own faults, he must depend on loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler wishes to know his own faults, he must rely on loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 苟其君愎諫自賢，其臣阿諛順旨，君既失國，臣豈能獨全！

translations.literal: If the ruler rejects remonstrance and deems himself wise, while his ministers flatter and follow his wishes, once the ruler has lost the state, how can the ministers alone remain intact!
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler rejects counsel and considers himself wise, while his ministers fawn and follow his every wish, once the ruler loses the realm, how can his ministers alone escape ruin!

sentences.zh: 如虞世基等諂事煬帝以保富貴，煬帝既弒，世基等亦誅。

translations.literal: Like Yu Shiji and others, who fawned on Emperor Yang to preserve wealth and rank—when Emperor Yang was assassinated, Shiji and the rest were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yu Shiji and his like, who flattered Emperor Yang to preserve their wealth and rank—when Yang was killed, Shiji and the others were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 公輩宜用此為戒，事有得失，無毋盡言！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen should take this as a warning: when affairs have right and wrong, do not fail to speak your mind fully!"
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen should heed this warning: when affairs go right or wrong, do not hold back—speak your minds fully!"

sentences.zh: 或上言秦府舊兵，宜盡除武職，追入宿衛。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized that former soldiers of the Prince of Qin's household should all be stripped of military posts and recalled to serve as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Someone suggested that all former soldiers of the Prince of Qin's household should be removed from military posts and recalled to palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 上謂之曰：「朕以天下為家，惟賢是與，豈舊兵之外皆無可信者乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to him: "I take all under Heaven as my household and give office only to the worthy—are there truly no trustworthy men beyond the old soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong replied: "I take the realm as my household and appoint only the worthy—do you mean there is no one trustworthy outside the old guard!

sentences.zh: 汝之此意，非所以廣朕德於天下也。」

translations.literal: Your idea is not the way to spread my virtue throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Such thinking is not how to extend my virtue across the realm."

sentences.zh: 上謂公卿曰：「昔禹鑿山治水而民無謗讟者，與人同利故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong told the high officials: "In antiquity Yu cut through mountains to control the waters, and the people had no slander or complaint—because he shared benefit with others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told the chief ministers: "In antiquity Yu cut through mountains to tame the floods, and the people did not murmur against him—because he shared their interests.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇營宮室而民怨叛者，病人以利己故也。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin built palaces and halls, the people resented and rebelled—because he harmed others to benefit himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Emperor of Qin built palaces, the people turned resentful and rebelled—because he harmed others to enrich himself.

sentences.zh: 夫靡麗珍奇，固人之所欲，若縱之不已，則危亡立至。

translations.literal: Luxury, splendor, and rare treasures are indeed what people desire; but if one indulges them without end, ruin arrives at once.
translations.idiomatic: Splendor and rare treasures are what people naturally desire—but if indulged without limit, disaster follows swiftly.

sentences.zh: 朕欲營一殿，材用已具，鑒秦而止。

translations.literal: I wished to build one hall; the materials were already prepared, but taking Qin as a warning, I stopped.
translations.idiomatic: I had intended to build a hall and the materials were already assembled, but taking Qin's example as a warning, I halted.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，宜體朕此意。」

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward, you ought to embrace this intention of mine."
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes downward, you should share this resolve of mine."

sentences.zh: 由是二十年間，風俗素樸，衣無錦繡，公私富給。

translations.literal: From this, over twenty years customs remained plain and simple; clothing had no brocade or embroidery, and both public and private stores were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, for twenty years customs stayed plain; clothing bore no brocade or embroidery, and both public and private coffers prospered.

sentences.zh: 上謂黃門侍郎王珪曰：「國家本置中書、門下以相檢察，中書詔敕或有差失，則門下當行駁正。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Gui: "The state originally established the Secretariat and the Chancellery to inspect each other; if an edict or order from the Secretariat has any error, the Chancellery should issue a rebuttal and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Gui: "The state established the Secretariat and the Chancellery to check each other; when a Secretariat edict contains an error, the Chancellery should reject and correct it.

sentences.zh: 人心所見，互有不同，苟論難往來，務求至當，捨己從人，亦復何傷！

translations.literal: What different minds see differs from one another; if debate and dispute go back and forth, striving for what is most fitting—abandoning one's own view to follow another's—what harm is there!
translations.idiomatic: Men see things differently; if debate goes back and forth in pursuit of what is right, yielding one's own view to another's—what injury is there in that!

sentences.zh: 比來或護己之短，遂成怨隙，或苟避私怨，知非不正，順一人顏情，為兆民之深患，此乃亡國之政也。

translations.literal: Lately some have shielded their own shortcomings and thereby created rancor and estrangement, or have avoided private resentments and, knowing what is wrong, failed to correct it, indulging one man's face and feelings—making a deep calamity for the myriad people; this is the governance that destroys states.
translations.idiomatic: Lately some have guarded their own flaws and bred resentment, or shunned private grudges and, knowing what is wrong, failed to set it right—indulging one man's feelings at the cost of the people. That is the kind of government that destroys a state.

sentences.zh: 煬帝之世，內外庶官，務相順從，當是之時，皆自謂有智，禍不及身。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time, officials within and without all strove to defer to one another; at that time each thought himself wise and that disaster would not reach his person.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Yang's reign, officials inside and outside court all strove to defer to one another; each thought himself clever and that calamity would never touch him.

sentences.zh: 及天下大亂，家國兩亡，雖其間萬一有得免者，亦為時論所貶，終古不磨。

translations.literal: When all under Heaven fell into great disorder and both family and state perished together, even if here and there one happened to escape, he was still condemned by contemporary opinion—a stain that never fades through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm collapsed and families and states perished together, even the rare man who escaped was condemned by his contemporaries—a stain that endures forever.

sentences.zh: 卿曹各當徇公忘私，勿雷同也！」

translations.literal: You all ought each to serve the public and forget the private; do not echo one another!"
translations.idiomatic: Each of you should serve the public interest and set private concerns aside—do not simply echo one another!"

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「吾聞西域賈胡得美珠，剖身以藏之，有諸？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to his attending ministers: "I have heard that a merchant from the Western Regions obtained a fine pearl and cut open his body to hide it inside—is this so?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong asked his attendants: "I have heard that a merchant from the Western Regions obtained a fine pearl and slit open his body to conceal it—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 侍臣曰：「有之。」

translations.literal: The attendants said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The attendants answered: "It is so."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「人皆知彼之愛珠而不愛其身也；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "All men know that he loved the pearl and did not love his own person;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "Everyone knows he loved the pearl more than his own life;

sentences.zh: 吏受賕抵法，與帝王徇奢欲而亡國者，何以異於彼胡之可笑邪！」

translations.literal: Officials who accept bribes and violate the law, and emperors who indulge extravagant desires and lose their states—how are they different from that laughable barbarian!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet how is an official who takes bribes and breaks the law, or an emperor who indulges luxury and loses his realm, any different from that ridiculous foreigner!"

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「昔魯哀公謂孔子曰：『人有好忘者，徙宅而忘其妻。』

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "In antiquity Duke Ai of Lu said to Confucius: 'There are men so forgetful that they move house and forget their wives.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said: "Long ago Duke Ai of Lu told Confucius: 'Some men are so forgetful they move house and forget their wives.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『又有甚者，桀、紂乃忘其身。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'There are worse cases still—Jie and Zhou forgot their own persons.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius replied: 'There are worse cases—Jie and Zhou forgot themselves entirely.'

sentences.zh: 亦猶是也。」

translations.literal: It is much the same here."
translations.idiomatic: The same applies here."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "True.

sentences.zh: 朕與公輩宜戮力相輔，庶免為人所笑也！」

translations.literal: I and you gentlemen ought to join our strength in mutual support, so that we may hopefully avoid being laughed at by others!"
translations.idiomatic: You and I should join our strength in mutual support, so that we may avoid becoming objects of ridicule!"

sentences.zh: 青州有謀反者，州縣逮捕支黨，收系滿獄，詔殿中侍御史安喜崔仁師覆按之。

translations.literal: In Qing Prefecture there were men plotting rebellion; the prefecture and counties arrested their associates and partisans until the prisons were full. An edict ordered Palace Attendant Censor Cui Renshi of Anxi to reinvestigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels were discovered in Qing Prefecture, local officials arrested their associates until the jails were overflowing. The emperor ordered Palace Attendant Censor Cui Renshi of Anxi to review the case.

sentences.zh: 仁師至，悉脫去杻械，與飲食湯沐，寬慰之，止坐其魁首十餘人，餘皆釋之。

translations.literal: When Renshi arrived, he had all shackles removed, gave them food, drink, and bathing, comforted them, and punished only the ringleaders—more than ten men—releasing all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Renshi arrived, he had all shackles removed, provided food, drink, and bathing, and reassured the prisoners; he punished only the dozen-odd ringleaders and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 還報，敕使將往決之。

translations.literal: He returned to report, and an imperial commissioner was sent to carry out the sentences.
translations.idiomatic: He reported back, and an imperial commissioner was dispatched to execute the sentences.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿孫伏伽謂仁師曰：「足下平反者多，人情誰不貪生，恐見徒侶得免，未肯甘心，深為足下憂之。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Sun Fuga said to Renshi: "You have exonerated many; among men, who does not cling to life? I fear that when they see their fellows go free, they will not be willing to accept it—I am deeply worried on your account."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Sun Fuga warned Renshi: "You have cleared many prisoners; who among men does not cling to life? I fear that when they see their fellows go free, they will refuse to accept guilt—I worry deeply for you."

sentences.zh: 仁師曰：「凡治獄當以平恕為本，豈可自規免罪，知其冤而不為伸邪！

translations.literal: Renshi said: "In handling cases one should take fairness and clemency as the foundation—how can one scheme to save oneself from punishment and, knowing men are wronged, fail to vindicate them!
translations.idiomatic: Renshi replied: "In judging cases one must take fairness and mercy as the foundation—how can I scheme to save my own skin and, knowing men are wronged, fail to vindicate them!

sentences.zh: 萬一暗短，誤有所縱，以一身易十囚之死，亦所願也。」

translations.literal: If by some hidden fault I err and release someone wrongly, to exchange my one person for the deaths of ten prisoners is also what I would wish."
translations.idiomatic: If through some blind error I release the wrong man, I would gladly trade my own life for the deaths of ten prisoners."

sentences.zh: 伏伽慚而退。

translations.literal: Fuga withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Fuga withdrew, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 及敕使至，更訊諸囚，皆曰：「崔公平恕，事無枉濫，請速就死。」

translations.literal: When the imperial commissioner arrived and questioned the prisoners again, all said: "Cui is fair and clement; in the affair there was no wrongful punishment—we ask only to die quickly."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial commissioner arrived and questioned the prisoners again, all said: "Cui was fair and merciful; no innocent man was punished—we ask only to die at once."

sentences.zh: 無一人異辭者。

translations.literal: Not one man gave a different account.
translations.idiomatic: Not one prisoner gave a different account.

sentences.zh: 上好騎射，孫伏伽諫，以為：「天子居則九門，行則警蹕，非欲苟自尊嚴，乃為社稷生民之計也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong loved riding and archery. Sun Fuga remonstrated, saying: "When the Son of Heaven dwells, there are the nine gates; when he travels, the road is cleared by escort—not because he wishes casually to aggrandize his dignity, but because it is a plan for the altars of state and the living people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong loved riding and archery. Sun Fuga remonstrated: "When the Son of Heaven dwells within the nine gates and travels with imperial escort, it is not mere vanity—it is for the sake of the realm and the people.

sentences.zh: 陛下好自走馬射的以娛悅近臣，此乃少年為諸王時所為，非今日天子事業也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty delights in riding at full gallop and shooting at targets to amuse your close ministers—this is what you did in youth when you were one of the princes; it is not the business of the Son of Heaven today.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty delights in galloping and shooting at targets to amuse your close attendants—this is what you did as a young prince, not what the emperor of today should be about.

sentences.zh: 既非所以安養聖躬，又非所以儀刑後世，臣竊為陛下不取。」

translations.literal: It is neither the way to nurture the sacred person in peace nor the way to set an example for later ages—I privately consider it unworthy of Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: It is neither the way to preserve Your Majesty's health nor the way to set an example for posterity—I cannot approve of it."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以伏伽為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Before long, Fuga was appointed Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Fuga was appointed Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 隋世選人，十一月集，至春而罷，人患其期促。

translations.literal: In Sui times, candidates for office assembled in the eleventh month and were dismissed in spring; people complained that the period was too short.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, examination candidates assembled in the eleventh month and were dismissed in spring; people complained the season was too brief.

sentences.zh: 至是，吏部侍郎觀城劉林甫奏四時聽選，隨闕注擬，人以為便。

translations.literal: At this time, Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office Liu Linpu of Guancheng memorialized that selections be heard in all four seasons, with appointments made as vacancies arose; people considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Vice Minister of Personnel Liu Linpu of Guancheng proposed holding selections in all four seasons and filling vacancies as they arose; people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 唐初，士大夫以亂離之後，不樂仕進，官員不充。

translations.literal: In early Tang, after the chaos and dispersal, gentry and officials were unwilling to pursue office; posts were unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang, after years of chaos and displacement, scholars were reluctant to enter government service, and offices went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 省符下諸州差人赴選，州府及詔使多以赤牒補官。

translations.literal: Provincial orders went down to the prefectures to dispatch men to selection; prefectures and imperial commissioners often used red writs to fill offices provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: Central orders went out to the prefectures to send candidates for selection, but prefectural officials and imperial commissioners often filled posts with provisional red writ appointments.

sentences.zh: 至是盡省之，勒赴省選，集者七千餘人，林甫隨才銓敘，各得其所，時人稱之。

translations.literal: At this time all such appointments were abolished, and men were compelled to come to the capital for selection; more than seven thousand assembled. Linpu assessed talent and assigned ranks so that each found his proper place; people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Now all such appointments were abolished and men were required to come to the capital for selection; more than seven thousand assembled. Linpu evaluated them by merit and placed each in his proper post; contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 詔以關中米貴，始分人於洛州選。

translations.literal: An edict was issued that because grain was dear in Guanzhong, candidates were for the first time divided and selected at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain was expensive in Guanzhong, an edict ordered candidates to be selected in part at Luoyang for the first time.

sentences.zh: 上謂房玄齡曰：「官在得人，不在員多。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to Fang Xuanling: "Office lies in getting the right men, not in having many posts."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told Fang Xuanling: "Government depends on finding the right men, not on filling many posts."

sentences.zh: 命玄齡並省，留文武總六百四十三員。

translations.literal: He ordered Xuanling to consolidate and reduce offices, retaining six hundred forty-three civil and military posts in all.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xuanling to consolidate offices, leaving six hundred forty-three civil and military posts in all.

sentences.zh: 隋秘書監晉陵劉子翼，有學行，性剛直，朋友有過，常面責之。

translations.literal: Liu Ziyi of Jinling, former Director of the Secretariat under Sui, had learning and conduct; his nature was stern and upright—when friends had faults, he often reproved them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziyi of Jinling, former Sui Director of the Secretariat, was a learned and upright man of stern character; when friends erred, he often rebuked them to their faces.

sentences.zh: 李百藥常稱：「劉四雖復罵人，人終不恨。」

translations.literal: Li Baiyao often praised him: "Though Liu the Fourth scolds people, in the end they bear no resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Li Baiyao often said: "Though Liu the Fourth scolds people, they never resent him in the end."

sentences.zh: 是歲，有詔征之，辭以母老，不至。

translations.literal: That year there was an edict summoning him; he declined on the grounds that his mother was old, and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was summoned by imperial edict, but declined on account of his aged mother and did not come.

sentences.zh: 鄃令裴仁軌私役門夫，上怒，欲斬之。

translations.literal: Pei Rengui, magistrate of Yu County, privately conscripted gate guards for labor. Emperor Taizong was angry and wished to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Rengui, magistrate of Yu County, had illegally conscripted gate guards for private labor. Emperor Taizong was furious and wanted him executed.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史長安李乾祐諫曰：「法者，陛下所與天下共也，非陛下所獨有也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Li Qianyou of Chang'an remonstrated: "The law is what Your Majesty shares with all under Heaven—it is not something Your Majesty alone possesses.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Li Qianyou of Chang'an remonstrated: "The law is what Your Majesty shares with the realm—it is not Your Majesty's alone.

sentences.zh: 今仁軌坐輕罪而抵極刑，臣恐人無所措手足。」

translations.literal: Now Rengui is guilty of a light offense yet faces the extreme penalty—I fear men will have nowhere to set hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: Rengui is guilty of a minor offense yet faces death—I fear people will not know where to stand."

sentences.zh: 上悅，免仁軌死，以乾祐為侍御史。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, spared Rengui from death, and appointed Qianyou Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was pleased, spared Rengui from death, and appointed Qianyou Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 上嘗語及關中、山東人，意有同異。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once spoke of men from Guanzhong and Shandong, his meaning showing partiality between them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once spoke of men from Guanzhong and Shandong in terms that suggested a distinction between them.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史義豐張行成跪奏曰：「天子以四海為家，不當有東西之異；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Xingcheng of Yifeng submitted kneeling: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his household—there ought not to be an east-west distinction;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Xingcheng of Yifeng knelt and submitted: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his household—there should be no east-west distinction;

sentences.zh: 恐示人以隘。」

translations.literal: I fear it shows men a narrow mind."
translations.idiomatic: I fear it shows the world a narrow mind."

sentences.zh: 上善其言，厚賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong approved and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 自是每有大政，常使預議。

translations.literal: From this on, whenever there was a major policy matter, he was regularly allowed to take part in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever major policy was debated, Zhang was regularly invited to participate.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥既強，敕勒諸部分散，有薛延陀、回紇、都播、骨利干、多濫葛、同羅、僕固、拔野古、思結、渾、斛薛、結、阿跌、契苾、白□等十五部，皆居磧北，風俗大抵與突厥同；

translations.literal: Initially, after the Turks had grown strong, the Tiele tribes were scattered. There were the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Dubo, Guligan, Duolangge, Tongluo, Pugu, Bayegu, Sijie, Hun, Huxue, Jie, Adie, Qibi, Bai Xi, and others—fifteen tribes in all—all dwelling north of the desert; their customs were largely the same as the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Turks had grown powerful, the Tiele tribes were scattered among fifteen groups—the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Dubo, Guligan, Duolan Ge, Tongluo, Pugu, Bayegu, Sijie, Hun, Huxue, Xi Jie, Adie, Qibi, Bai Xi, and others—all living north of the desert, their customs largely matching those of the Turks;

sentences.zh: 薛延陀於諸部為最強。

translations.literal: Among all the tribes, the Xueyantuo were the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the tribes, the Xueyantuo were the strongest.

sentences.zh: 西突厥曷薩那可汗方強，敕勒諸部皆臣之。

translations.literal: The Western Turk qaghan Yeshana was then strong, and all the Tiele tribes submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk qaghan Yeshana was then at the height of his power, and all the Tiele tribes submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 曷薩那徵稅無度，諸部皆怨。

translations.literal: Yeshana levied taxes without limit, and all the tribes resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yeshana levied taxes without limit, and every tribe resented him.

sentences.zh: 曷薩那誅其渠帥百餘人，敕勒相帥叛之，共推契苾哥楞為易勿真莫賀可汗，居貪於山北。

translations.literal: Yeshana executed more than a hundred of their chieftains. The Tiele led one another in rebellion against him and jointly enthroned Qibi Geleng as Yiwuzhen Mohe Qaghan, dwelling north of Mount Tanju.
translations.idiomatic: Yeshana executed more than a hundred of their chieftains. The Tiele rose in rebellion under their leaders and jointly enthroned Qibi Geleng as Yiwuzhen Mohe Qaghan, with his seat north of Mount Tanju.

sentences.zh: 又以薛延陀乙失缽為也咥小可汗，居燕末山北。

translations.literal: They also made Yishibo of the Xueyantuo Yedie Lesser Qaghan, dwelling north of Mount Yanmo.
translations.idiomatic: They also made Yishibo of the Xueyantuo the Yedie Lesser Qaghan, with his seat north of Mount Yanmo.

sentences.zh: 及射匱可汗兵復振，薛延陀、契苾二部並去可汗之號以臣之。

translations.literal: When Qaghan Shegui's armies revived in strength, the Xueyantuo and Qibi tribes both cast off their qaghan titles and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qaghan Shegui's armies regained their strength, the Xueyantuo and Qibi both renounced their qaghan titles and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 回紇等六部在郁督軍山者，東屬始畢可汗。

translations.literal: The six tribes including the Huihe, dwelling at Mount Yudujun, submitted to the east to Qaghan Shibi.
translations.idiomatic: The six tribes including the Huihe, who lived at Mount Yudujun, submitted to Qaghan Shibi in the east.

sentences.zh: 統葉護可汗勢衰，乙失缽之孫夷男帥其部落七萬餘家，附於頡利可汗。

translations.literal: When Qaghan Tongyehu's power declined, Yishibo's grandson Yinan led his tribe of more than seventy thousand households and attached himself to Qaghan Jiali.
translations.idiomatic: When Qaghan Tongyehu's power waned, Yishibo's grandson Yinan led his tribe of more than seventy thousand households and submitted to Qaghan Jiali.

sentences.zh: 頡利政亂，薛延陀與回紇、拔野古等相帥叛之。

translations.literal: Jiali's government fell into disorder; the Xueyantuo, together with the Huihe, Bayegu, and others, led one another in rebellion against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali's rule fell into disorder, and the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Bayegu, and others rose in rebellion under their leaders.

sentences.zh: 頡利遣其兄子欲谷設將十萬騎討之，回紇酋長菩薩將五千騎，與戰於馬鬣山，大破之。

translations.literal: Jiali sent his elder brother's son Yugu She at the head of one hundred thousand horsemen to suppress them. The Huihe chieftain Pusa led five thousand horsemen and fought them at Mount Majie, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali sent his nephew Yugu She with one hundred thousand horsemen to suppress them. The Huihe chieftain Pusa led five thousand riders and routed them at Mount Majie.

sentences.zh: 欲谷設走，菩薩追至天山，部眾多為所虜，回紇由是大振。

translations.literal: Yugu She fled; Pusa pursued him to Mount Tianshan, and many of his followers were captured. From this the Huihe grew greatly in power.
translations.idiomatic: Yugu She fled; Pusa pursued him to the Tianshan range, capturing many of his followers. The Huihe thereby rose to great prominence.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀又破其四設，頡利不能制。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo also defeated his four she; Jiali could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo also defeated his four military governors, and Jiali could no longer control them.

sentences.zh: 頡利益衰，國人離散。

translations.literal: Jiali declined further, and his people dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali's power waned further, and his people scattered.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，平地數尺，羊馬多死，民大饑，頡利恐唐乘其弊，引兵入朔州境上，揚言會獵，實設備焉。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy snow fell, several chi deep on level ground; many sheep and horses died, and the people suffered great famine. Jiali feared Tang would take advantage of his weakness, led troops into the borderlands of Shuozhou, declared a hunting assembly, but in reality made defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell, burying the plains several chi deep; countless sheep and horses perished, and famine spread among the people. Fearing that Tang would exploit his weakness, Jiali led troops to the border of Shuozhou, proclaiming a hunting expedition while in fact preparing for defense.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚卿鄭元□使突厥還。

translations.literal: Court of Diplomatic Reception Director Zheng Yuansui, having been sent as envoy to the Turks, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuansui, Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, returned from his mission to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 言於上曰：「戎狄興衰，專以羊馬為侯。

translations.literal: He said to the emperor: "The rise and fall of the Rong and Di depend solely on sheep and horses as their signs.
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor: "For the barbarians of the north, prosperity and decline are read entirely in the condition of their sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 今突厥民饑畜瘦，此將亡之兆也，不過三年。」

translations.literal: Now the Turks' people are starving and their livestock lean—this is a sign that they are about to perish, within no more than three years."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Turks are starving and their herds are wasted thin. This is a sign they are nearing collapse—within three years at most."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 群臣多勸上乘間擊突厥，上曰：「新與人盟而背之，不信；

translations.literal: Many among the ministers urged the emperor to seize the opportunity and strike the Turks. The emperor said: "Having just made an alliance with others and then turning against it is untrustworthy;
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers urged the emperor to strike the Turks while they were weak. The emperor said: "To make a fresh alliance and then betray it would be faithless;

sentences.zh: 利人之災，不仁；

translations.literal: to profit from another's disaster is unkind;
translations.idiomatic: to profit from another's disaster would be unkind;

sentences.zh: 乘人之危以取勝，不武。

translations.literal: to take advantage of another's peril to win victory is unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: to seize victory by exploiting another's distress would be unworthy.

sentences.zh: 縱使其種落盡叛，六畜無餘，朕終不擊，必待有罪，然後討之。」

translations.literal: Even if every one of their tribes should rebel away and their six kinds of livestock be utterly exhausted, I still will not strike. I must wait until they have committed offense, and only then punish them."
translations.idiomatic: Even if every tribe deserted them and not a head of livestock remained, I still would not attack. I will wait until they give cause for offense, and only then move against them."

sentences.zh: 西突厥統葉護可汗遣真珠統俟斤與高平王道立來，獻萬釘寶鈿金帶，馬五千匹，以迎公主。

translations.literal: The Western Turk qaghan Tong Yehu sent Zhenzhu, a tonghou commander, together with Prince of Gaoping Dao Li, bearing a gold belt studded with ten thousand jewels, five thousand horses, to welcome the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk qaghan Tong Yehu sent the tonghou commander Zhenzhu and Prince of Gaoping Dao Li with a gold belt set with ten thousand jeweled studs and five thousand horses to escort the princess.

sentences.zh: 頡利不欲中國與之和親，數遣兵入寇，又遣人謂統葉護曰：「汝迎唐公主，要須經我國中過。」

translations.literal: Jiali did not wish China to make a marriage alliance with him. He repeatedly sent troops to raid the borders, and also sent a man to tell Tong Yehu: "When you welcome the Tang princess, you must pass through my territory."
translations.idiomatic: Jiali did not want China to ally with Tong Yehu by marriage. He repeatedly sent raiders across the border and also sent word to Tong Yehu: "If you are to escort the Tang princess, you must pass through my lands."

sentences.zh: 統葉護患之，未成昏。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu was troubled by this, and the marriage was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu was alarmed, and the marriage never took place.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，右僕射長孫無忌罷。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day xinhai, Right Vice Director Zhangsun Wuji was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day xinhai of the first month, Right Vice Director Zhangsun Wuji was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時有密表稱無忌權寵過盛者，上以表示之，曰：「朕於卿洞然無疑，若各懷所聞而不言，則君臣之意有不通。」

translations.literal: At the time there were secret memorials saying that Wuji's power and favor were excessive. The emperor showed him the memorials and said: "Toward you I am utterly clear and without doubt. If each of us keeps what he has heard and does not speak, then the understanding between ruler and minister will not be complete."
translations.idiomatic: Secret memorials had accused Wuji of holding excessive power and favor. The emperor showed him the reports and said: "I harbor no doubt about you whatsoever. If each of us keeps what he hears to himself and says nothing, ruler and minister will fail to understand one another."

sentences.zh: 又召百官謂之曰：「朕諸子皆幼，視無忌如子，非他人所能間也。」

translations.literal: He also summoned all the officials and said to them: "My sons are all still young. I regard Wuji as a son; no one else can come between us."
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the entire court and said: "My sons are still young. I regard Wuji as one of my own children, and no outsider can drive us apart."

sentences.zh: 無忌自懼滿盈，固求遜位，皇后又力為之請，上乃許之，以為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wuji himself feared that he had reached the full measure of honor, and firmly requested to yield his post. The empress also pressed the request on his behalf, and the emperor then consented, appointing him Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji, fearing he had risen too high, repeatedly asked to step down. The empress pressed the request as well, and the emperor finally agreed, appointing him Kaifu Yitong Sansi.

sentences.zh: 置六司侍郎，副六尚書；

translations.literal: Six bureau vice directors were established to assist the six ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Six bureau vice directors were created to assist the six ministers;

sentences.zh: 並置左右司郎中各一人。

translations.literal: and one Left Bureau director and one Right Bureau director were also established.
translations.idiomatic: and one director each was appointed to the Left and Right Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，吐谷渾寇岷州，都督李道彥擊走之。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Tuyuhun raided Min Prefecture. Protector-general Li Daoyan struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Tuyuhun raided Min Prefecture. Protector-general Li Daoyan repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，徙漢王恪為蜀王，衛王泰為越王，楚王祐為燕王。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Prince of Han Ke was transferred to Prince of Shu, Prince of Wei Tai to Prince of Yue, and Prince of Chu You to Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Prince Ke of Han was made Prince of Shu, Prince Tai of Wei was made Prince of Yue, and Prince You of Chu was made Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 上問魏徵曰：「人主何為而明，何為而暗？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wei Zheng: "What makes a ruler enlightened, and what makes him benighted?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei Zheng: "What makes a ruler clear-sighted, and what makes him blind?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「兼聽則明，偏信則暗。

translations.literal: He replied: "To listen broadly is to be enlightened; to believe one-sidedly is to be benighted.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Listen to many voices and you will see clearly; trust only one side and you will be blind.

sentences.zh: 昔堯清問下民，故有苗之惡得以上聞；

translations.literal: In antiquity Yao made clear inquiry among the common people, and so the evil of the Miao was able to reach his ears above;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Yao sought honest reports from the people below, and so the crimes of the Miao reached his ears;

sentences.zh: 舜明四目，達四聰，故共、鯀、歡兜不能蔽也。

translations.literal: Shun had four eyes made clear and four ears made penetrating, and so Gong, Gun, and Huan Dou could not conceal themselves from him.
translations.idiomatic: Shun kept his four eyes clear and his four ears open, and so Gong, Gun, and Huan Dou could not hide the truth from him.

sentences.zh: 秦二世偏信趙高，以成望夷之禍；

translations.literal: Qin Er Shi believed only Zhao Gao, and thereby brought on the disaster at Wangyi;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Er Shi trusted Zhao Gao alone and brought on the disaster at Wangyi;

sentences.zh: 梁武帝偏信朱異，以取台城之辱；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang believed only Zhu Yi, and thereby suffered the humiliation at Taicheng;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang trusted Zhu Yi alone and suffered the humiliation at Taicheng;

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝偏信虞世基，以致彭城閣之變。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui believed only Yu Shiji, and thereby met the upheaval at the Pengcheng Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui trusted Yu Shiji alone and met the mutiny at the Pengcheng Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 是故人君兼聽廣納，則貴臣不得擁蔽，而下情得以上通也。」

translations.literal: Therefore when a ruler listens broadly and accepts widely, eminent ministers cannot block and conceal, and conditions below are able to reach upward."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when a ruler listens widely and accepts counsel from many quarters, powerful ministers cannot conceal the truth, and the voices of the people can reach the throne."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Well said!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 上謂黃門侍郎王珪曰：「開皇十四年大旱，隋文帝不許賑給，而令百姓就食山東，比至末年，天下儲積可供五十年。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yellow Gate Vice Director Wang Gui: "In the fourteenth year of Kaihuang there was a great drought. Emperor Wen of Sui would not permit relief distribution, but ordered the people to go eat in Shandong. By the end of his reign, the stored grain throughout the realm could supply fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yellow Gate Vice Director Wang Gui: "In Kaihuang 14 there was a severe drought. Emperor Wen of Sui refused direct relief and instead told the people to go find food in Shandong. By the end of his reign the empire's granaries held enough for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 煬帝恃其富饒，侈心無厭，卒亡天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang relied on that wealth and abundance; his appetite for extravagance knew no limit, and in the end he lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang counted on that abundance, indulged his appetite for luxury without end, and in the end lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 但使倉廩之積足以備凶年，其餘何用哉！」

translations.literal: If only the stores in the granaries are sufficient to prepare for bad years, what use is the rest!"
translations.idiomatic: If the granaries hold enough to see us through famine years, what need is there for more!"

sentences.zh: 二月，上謂侍臣曰：「人言天子至尊，無所畏憚。

translations.literal: Second month: the emperor said to his attending ministers: "People say the Son of Heaven is supreme and has nothing to fear or dread.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor told his ministers: "People say the Son of Heaven stands above all and has nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 朕則不然，上畏皇天之監臨，下憚群臣之瞻仰，兢兢業業，猶恐不合天意，未副人望。」

translations.literal: I am not so. Above I fear the oversight of August Heaven; below I dread the gaze of the ministers. Diligent and careful, I still fear that I do not accord with Heaven's intent and fail to fulfill men's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: I am not like that. Above, I fear Heaven's watchful eye; below, I dread the scrutiny of my ministers. I remain cautious and uneasy, still afraid that I fall short of Heaven's will and the people's hopes."

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「此誠致治之要，願陛下慎終如始，則善矣。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "This truly is the key to bringing about good order. I wish Your Majesty to be as careful at the end as at the beginning—then all will be well."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said: "That is indeed the heart of good governance. If Your Majesty remains as careful at the end as at the beginning, nothing more need be asked."

sentences.zh: 上謂房玄齡等曰：「為政莫若至公。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Fang Xuanling and the others: "In governing, nothing surpasses utmost impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Fang Xuanling and the others: "In governing, nothing surpasses complete impartiality.

sentences.zh: 昔諸葛亮竄廖立、李嚴於南夷，亮卒而立、嚴皆悲泣，有死者，非至公能如是乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity Zhuge Liang banished Liao Li and Li Yan to the southern barbarians. When Liang died, Li and Yan both wept in grief, and some died. Could anyone but one of utmost impartiality have achieved this!
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhuge Liang exiled Liao Li and Li Yan to the far south. When he died, both men wept in grief—some even died of grief. Only a man of absolute fairness could inspire that!

sentences.zh: 又高熲為隋相，公平識治體，隋之興亡，系熲之存沒。

translations.literal: Again, Gao Jiong served as Sui chancellor. Impartial and understanding the body of governance, Sui's rise and fall hung on whether Jiong lived or died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong too served as chancellor of Sui. Fair-minded and deeply versed in statecraft, the dynasty's rise and fall turned on whether he lived or died.

sentences.zh: 朕既慕前世之明君，卿等不可不法前世之賢相也。」

translations.literal: Since I already admire the enlightened rulers of former ages, you must not fail to take as your model the worthy chancellors of former ages."
translations.idiomatic: Since I admire the enlightened rulers of old, you must take the great chancellors of old as your model."

sentences.zh: 三月，戊寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Third month, on the first day wuyin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon of wuyin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 壬子，大理少卿胡演進每月囚帳；

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Hu Yan presented the monthly register of prisoners;
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Hu Yan presented the monthly prisoner register;

sentences.zh: 上命自今大辟皆令中書、門下四品已上及尚書議之，庶無冤濫。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered that from now on all capital cases must be deliberated by officials of fourth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery, together with the ministers, so that wrongful and excessive punishments might be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered that from then on every capital case be reviewed by fourth-rank officials and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery together with the ministers, so that injustice might be avoided.

sentences.zh: 既而引囚，至岐州刺史鄭善果，上謂胡演曰：「善果雖復有罪，官品不卑，豈可使與諸囚為伍。

translations.literal: Then the prisoners were led forward. When they reached Zheng Shanguo, prefect of Qi Prefecture, the emperor said to Hu Yan: "Although Shanguo has indeed committed offense, his official rank is not low. How can he be made to stand among the other prisoners?
translations.idiomatic: When the prisoners were led forward and Zheng Shanguo, prefect of Qi, appeared among them, the emperor told Hu Yan: "Shanguo may be guilty, but his rank is not low. How can he be paraded with common criminals?

sentences.zh: 自今三品以上犯罪，不須引過，聽於朝堂俟進止。」

translations.literal: From now on, when officials of third rank and above commit offense, they need not be led past in procession; let them wait in the court hall for the emperor's decision."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, officials of third rank and above who commit crimes need not be paraded through the streets; they may wait in the court hall for the emperor's decision."

sentences.zh: 關內旱饑，民多賣子以接衣食；

translations.literal: In Guannei there was drought and famine; many among the people sold their children to sustain food and clothing;
translations.idiomatic: Drought and famine struck Guannei, and many people sold their children to buy food and clothing;

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔出御府金帛為贖之，歸其父母。

translations.literal: on the day jisi, an edict ordered gold and silk from the imperial treasury to redeem them and return them to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: on jisi an edict ordered gold and silk from the imperial treasury used to redeem the children and return them to their parents.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔以去歲霖雨，今茲旱、蝗，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, an edict declared that because of last year's torrential rains and this year's drought and locusts, an amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu an edict declared a general amnesty, citing last year's floods and this year's drought and locust plague.

sentences.zh: 詔書略曰：「若使年谷豐稔，天下又安，移災朕身，以存萬國，是所願也，甘心無吝。」

translations.literal: The edict in summary said: "If only the year's grain were abundant and all under Heaven were at peace, I would shift the disaster onto my own person to preserve the myriad states—that is my wish, and I would do so gladly without regret."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read in part: "If only the harvest were rich and the realm at peace, I would gladly take these disasters upon myself to preserve the empire—that is my wish, without hesitation."

sentences.zh: 會所在有雨，民大悅。

translations.literal: Just then rain fell throughout the region, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell across the region, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己卯，詔以「隋末亂離，因之饑饉，暴骸滿野，傷人心目，宜令所在官司收瘞。」

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the day jimao, an edict declared: "At the end of Sui there was disorder and separation, followed by famine. Exposed corpses filled the fields, wounding the eyes and hearts of men. The local offices everywhere should be ordered to collect and bury them."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on jimao of the fourth month, an edict declared: "At the end of Sui, war and famine left exposed corpses strewn across the fields, a sight that wounds the heart. Local authorities everywhere are ordered to collect and bury the dead."

sentences.zh: 初，突厥突利可汗建牙直幽州之北，主東偏，奚、□等數十部多叛突厥來降，頡利可汗以其失眾責之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Turk qaghan Tuli had established his headquarters directly north of You Prefecture, governing the eastern sector. Dozens of tribes including the Xi and others mostly rebelled against the Turks and came to surrender. Jiali qaghan blamed him for losing his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Turk qaghan Tuli had set up his headquarters just north of You Prefecture, governing the eastern territories. Dozens of tribes, including the Xi and their allies, largely broke from the Turks and submitted to Tang. Jiali blamed Tuli for losing his followers.

sentences.zh: 及薛延陀、回紇等敗欲谷設，頡利遣突利討之，突利兵又敗，輕騎奔還。

translations.literal: When the Xueyantuo, Huihe, and others defeated Yugu She, Jiali sent Tuli to punish them. Tuli's army was again defeated, and he fled back with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xueyantuo, Huihe, and others defeated Yugu She, Jiali sent Tuli to punish them. Tuli's army was beaten again, and he fled back with a small escort.

sentences.zh: 頡利怒，拘之十餘日而撻之，突利由是怨，陰欲叛頡利。

translations.literal: Jiali was enraged, detained him for more than ten days, and whipped him. Tuli therefore resented him and secretly wished to rebel against Jiali.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali flew into a rage, held him for more than ten days, and had him whipped. Tuli nursed a grievance and secretly planned to break with Jiali.

sentences.zh: 頡利數徵兵於突利，突利不與，表請入朝。

translations.literal: Jiali repeatedly requisitioned troops from Tuli, but Tuli would not supply them and submitted a memorial requesting to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali repeatedly demanded troops from Tuli, but Tuli refused and petitioned to come to court in person.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「向者突厥之強，控弦百萬，憑陵中夏，用是驕恣，以失其民。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attending ministers: "Formerly the Turks were strong—a million bowmen—and they overawed the Central Lands. Because of this they grew arrogant and willful, and thereby lost the loyalty of their people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: "Once the Turks were strong— a million bowmen strong—and they lorded it over China. Pride led them to lose the loyalty of their people.

sentences.zh: 今自請入朝，非困窮，肯如是乎！

translations.literal: Now he asks of his own accord to come to court. If he were not in distress, would he do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: Now he asks to come to court of his own accord. Would he do that if he were not desperate!

sentences.zh: 朕聞之，且喜且懼。

translations.literal: When I hear this, I am both pleased and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When I hear this, I am both glad and afraid.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 突厥衰則邊境安矣，故喜。

translations.literal: If the Turks decline, the borders will be secure—therefore I am pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If the Turks weaken, the borders will be secure—that is why I am glad.

sentences.zh: 然朕或失道，它日亦將如突厥，能無懼乎！

translations.literal: Yet if I should lose the Way, one day I too will be like the Turks—how could I not be afraid!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I lose my way, one day I too may end up like the Turks—how could I not be afraid!

sentences.zh: 卿曹宜不惜苦諫，以輔朕之不逮也。」

translations.literal: You all ought not to spare yourselves hard remonstrance, to assist where I fall short."
translations.idiomatic: You must not spare me hard counsel, to help me where I fall short."

sentences.zh: 頡利發兵攻突利，丁亥，突利遣使來求救。

translations.literal: Jiali sent troops to attack Tuli. On the day dinghai, Tuli dispatched an envoy to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali sent troops against Tuli. On dinghai, Tuli sent an envoy begging for help.

sentences.zh: 上謀於大臣曰：「朕與突利為兄弟，有急不可不救。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted the great ministers and said: "Tuli and I are sworn brothers. When he is in distress I cannot fail to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his senior ministers and said: "Tuli and I are sworn brothers. I cannot leave him in distress.

sentences.zh: 然頡利亦與之有盟，奈何？」

translations.literal: Yet Jiali also has an alliance with him—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiali too is bound to him by alliance. What then?"

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書杜如晦曰：「戎狄無信，終當負約，今不因其亂而取之，後悔無及。

translations.literal: Minister of War Du Ruhui said: "The Rong and Di are without trust and will ultimately break their pledges. If we do not take advantage of their disorder to seize the opportunity now, later we will regret it with no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Du Ruhui said: "The barbarians are faithless and will break their pledges in the end. If we do not seize this disorder now, we will regret it too late.

sentences.zh: 夫取亂侮亡，古之道也。」

translations.literal: To take advantage of disorder and strike a declining state—this is the way of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: To strike a state in chaos and exploit its decline—that is the ancient way."

sentences.zh: 丙申，契丹酋長帥其部落來降。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, a Khitan chieftain led his tribe to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen a Khitan chieftain led his tribe in submission.

sentences.zh: 頡利遣使請以梁師都易契丹，上謂使者曰：「契丹與突厥異類，今來歸附，何故索之！

translations.literal: Jiali sent an envoy requesting to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan. The emperor said to the envoy: "The Khitan and the Turks are of different kind. Now that they have come to submit, why demand them back!
translations.idiomatic: Jiali sent an envoy offering to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan. The emperor told the envoy: "The Khitan and the Turks are not the same people. They have just submitted to us—why should I hand them over!

sentences.zh: 師都中國之人，盜我土地，暴我百姓，突厥受而庇之，我興兵致討，輒來救之，彼如魚游釜中，何患不為我有！

translations.literal: Shidu is a man of China who stole our lands and brutalized our people. The Turks received and sheltered him. When I raised troops to punish him, they came at once to rescue him. He is like a fish swimming in a cauldron—what worry is there that he will not become mine!
