translations.idiomatic: Shidu is one of our own people who seized our territory and preyed on our people, yet the Turks took him in. When I sent troops to punish him, they rushed to his rescue. He is like a fish in a boiling pot—why should I worry that he will not soon be mine!

sentences.zh: 借使不得，亦終不以降附之民易之也。」

translations.literal: Even supposing I cannot obtain him, I still would never exchange people who have submitted for him."
translations.idiomatic: Even if I fail to take him, I will never trade away people who have submitted for him."

sentences.zh: 先是，上知突厥政亂，不能庇梁師都，以書諭之，師都不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor knew that Turk governance was in disorder and that they could not protect Liang Shidu. He sent a letter to instruct Shidu, but Shidu would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, knowing that Turk rule was in disarray and that they could no longer protect Liang Shidu, the emperor sent Shidu a letter urging surrender, but Shidu refused.

sentences.zh: 上遣夏州都督長史劉旻、司馬劉蘭成圖之，旻等數遣輕騎踐其禾稼，多縱反間，離其君臣，其國漸虛，降者相屬。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Chief Administrator Liu Min and Vice Administrator Liu Lancheng of Xia Prefecture to plot against him. Min and the others repeatedly sent light cavalry to trample his grain fields, spread many counter-intelligence schemes, and estrange ruler and ministers. His state gradually weakened, and those who surrendered followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Chief Administrator Liu Min and Vice Administrator Liu Lancheng of Xia Prefecture to undermine him. They repeatedly sent light cavalry to trample his crops, spread disinformation, and drive a wedge between Shidu and his followers. His state steadily weakened, and defectors came in one after another.

sentences.zh: 其名將李正寶等謀執師都，事洩，來奔，由是上下益相疑。

translations.literal: His famous general Li Zhengbao and others plotted to seize Shidu. The affair leaked out, and they fled to Tang. From this, those above and below grew ever more suspicious of one another.
translations.idiomatic: His leading general Li Zhengbao and others plotted to seize Shidu, but the plot leaked and they fled to Tang. From then on, mutual suspicion deepened throughout Shidu's camp.

sentences.zh: 旻等知可取，上表請兵。

translations.literal: Min and the others knew he could be taken and submitted a memorial requesting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Min and his colleagues judged that Shidu could be taken and petitioned for troops.

sentences.zh: 上遣右衛大將軍柴紹、殿中少監薛萬均擊之，又遣旻等據朔方東城以逼之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Right Guard General Chai Shao and Palace Supervisor Xue Wanjun to attack him, and also sent Min and the others to hold the eastern city of Shuofang to press him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Right Guard General Chai Shao and Palace Supervisor Xue Wanjun to attack him, and ordered Min and the others to hold the eastern city of Shuofang and tighten the pressure.

sentences.zh: 師都引突厥兵至城下，劉蘭成偃旗臥鼓不出。

translations.literal: Shidu led Turk troops to the foot of the city wall. Liu Lancheng lowered his banners, silenced his drums, and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu brought Turk troops to the walls of the eastern city. Liu Lancheng lowered his banners, silenced his drums, and lay low.

sentences.zh: 師都宵遁，蘭成追擊，破之。

translations.literal: Shidu fled by night. Lancheng pursued and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu fled by night. Lancheng pursued and routed him.

sentences.zh: 突厥大發兵救師都，柴紹等未至朔方數十里，與突厥遇，奮擊，大破之，遂圍朔方。

translations.literal: The Turks mobilized a large force to rescue Shidu. When Chai Shao and the others were still several tens of li from Shuofang, they encountered the Turks, struck fiercely, and routed them greatly, then besieged Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks sent a large relief force for Shidu. Still several tens of li from Shuofang, Chai Shao and his men met the Turks, fought fiercely, and routed them, then laid siege to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 突厥不敢救，城中食盡。

translations.literal: The Turks did not dare to rescue him, and food in the city was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks dared not attempt another rescue, and food in the city ran out.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，師都從父弟洛仁殺師都，以城降，以其地為夏州。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Shidu's younger cousin by the father's side Luoren killed Shidu and surrendered the city with it. The territory was made Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Shidu's cousin Luoren killed him and surrendered the city. The territory was reorganized as Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿祖孝孫以為梁、陳之音多吳、楚，周、齊之音多胡、夷，於是斟酌南北，考以古聲，作《唐雅樂》，凡八十四調、三十一曲、十二和。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun held that the music of Liang and Chen was largely Wu and Chu in character, while the music of Zhou and Qi was largely Hu and Yi in character. Thereupon he blended north and south, examined them against ancient tones, and composed the Tang Elegant Music—eighty-four modes, thirty-one pieces, and twelve he in all.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun argued that Liang and Chen music drew heavily on Wu and Chu styles, while Zhou and Qi music drew heavily on northern and foreign styles. He therefore blended northern and southern traditions, tested them against ancient pitch standards, and composed the Tang Elegant Music—eighty-four modes, thirty-one pieces, and twelve he in all.

sentences.zh: 詔協律郎張文收與孝孫同修定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pitch Regulation Director Zhang Wenshou to join Xiaosun in further revising and fixing it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Pitch Regulation Director Zhang Wenshou to join Xiaosun in completing the revision.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙酉，孝孫等奏新樂。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on the day yiyou, Xiaosun and the others presented the new music.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yiyou, Xiaosun and his colleagues presented the new music.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「禮樂者，蓋聖人緣情以設教耳，治之隆替，豈由於此？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Rites and music are simply what the sages established as teaching by following human feeling—can the rise and fall of governance really depend on this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Rites and music are merely what the sages devised to teach through human feeling—can the rise and fall of a dynasty really turn on that?"

sentences.zh: 御史大夫杜淹曰：「齊之將亡，作《伴侶曲》，陳之將亡，作《玉樹後庭花》，其聲哀思，行路聞之皆悲泣，何得言治之隆替不在樂也！」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan said: "When Qi was about to perish, it produced the Banlu Qu; when Chen was about to perish, it produced the Yushu Houting Hua. Their sounds were mournful and plaintive—passersby on the road who heard them all wept in grief. How can one say that the rise and fall of governance is not in music!"
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan said: "When Qi was near collapse it produced the Banlu Qu; when Chen was near collapse it produced the Yushu Houting Hua. Both were mournful—travelers who heard them wept in the streets. How can you say music has nothing to do with a dynasty's rise and fall!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 夫樂能感人，故樂者聞之則喜，憂者聞之則悲，悲喜在人心，非由樂也。

translations.literal: Music can move people. Therefore the joyful hear it and rejoice; the sorrowful hear it and grieve. Joy and grief lie in the human heart—they do not come from the music.
translations.idiomatic: Music moves people, it is true—the joyful hear it and rejoice, the sorrowful hear it and grieve. But joy and grief lie in the heart, not in the music itself.

sentences.zh: 將亡之政，民必愁苦，故聞樂而悲耳。

translations.literal: Under a government about to perish, the people must be full of grief and bitterness; that is why they hear music and grieve.
translations.idiomatic: When a regime is failing, the people are already full of grief—that is why they weep when they hear such music.

sentences.zh: 今二曲具存，朕為公奏之，公豈悲乎？」

translations.literal: Now both pieces still exist. If I play them for you, would you grieve?"
translations.idiomatic: Both pieces still exist. If I were to play them for you now, would you weep?"

sentences.zh: 右丞魏徵曰：「古人稱『禮雲禮雲，玉帛雲乎哉！

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Wei Zheng said: "The ancients said: 'Rites, rites—is it jade and silk?
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Wei Zheng said: "The ancients said: 'Rites, rites—is it merely jade and silk?

sentences.zh: 樂雲樂雲，鐘鼓雲乎哉！』

translations.literal: Music, music—is it bells and drums?'"
translations.idiomatic: Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?'"

sentences.zh: 樂誠在人和，不在聲音也。」

translations.literal: Music truly lies in harmony among people, not in sound itself."
translations.idiomatic: Music truly lies in harmony among people, not in the sounds themselves."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「臣聞垂能目制方圓，心度曲直，然不能以教人，其所以教人者，必規矩而已矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: "I have heard that Chui could with his eyes set square and round and in his heart measure crooked and straight, yet he could not use this to teach others; what he used to teach others was nothing but compass and square.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: "I have heard that Chui could judge square and round by eye and measure straight and crooked in his mind, yet he could not impart that skill directly to others; what he taught with was nothing but compass and square.

sentences.zh: 聖人不勉而中，不思而得，然不能以授人，其所以授人者，必禮樂而已矣。

translations.literal: The sage, without striving, hits the mark; without thinking, obtains it—yet cannot use this to impart to others; what he uses to impart to others is nothing but rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: The sage achieves the right without effort and attains understanding without deliberation, yet cannot pass that inner attainment directly to others; what he teaches with is rites and music alone.

sentences.zh: 禮者，聖人之所履也；

translations.literal: Rites are what the sage treads upon;
translations.idiomatic: Rites are what the sage walks in;

sentences.zh: 樂者，聖人之所樂也。

translations.literal: music is what the sage delights in.
translations.idiomatic: music is what the sage delights in.

sentences.zh: 聖人履中正而樂和平，又思與四海共之，百世傳之，於是乎作禮樂焉。

translations.literal: The sage treads centrality and rectitude and delights in peace and harmony, and also thinks to share it with all within the four seas and transmit it for a hundred generations—thereupon he composed rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: The sage walks in centrality and rectitude and delights in peace and harmony, and wished to share this with all within the four seas and pass it down for a hundred generations—thereupon he created rites and music.

sentences.zh: 故工人執垂之規矩而施之器，是亦垂之功已；

translations.literal: Thus when a craftsman takes Chui's compass and square and applies them to vessels, that is also Chui's achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when a craftsman takes Chui's compass and square and applies them to his work, that too is Chui's achievement;

sentences.zh: 王者執五帝、三王之禮樂而施之世，是亦五帝、三王之治已。

translations.literal: when a king takes the rites and music of the Five Emperors and Three Kings and applies them to the world, that is also the governance of the Five Emperors and Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: when a king takes up the rites and music of the Five Emperors and Three Kings and applies them to the realm, that too is the governance of the Five Emperors and Three Kings.

sentences.zh: 五帝、三王，其違世已久，後之人見其禮知其所履，聞其樂知其所樂，炳然若猶存於世焉。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors and Three Kings have long departed the world; later people who see their rites know what they trod upon, who hear their music know what they delighted in—it shines forth as if they still existed in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors and Three Kings have long since departed this world, yet later generations who see their rites know how they lived, and who hear their music know what they delighted in—it shines forth as if they were still among us.

sentences.zh: 此非禮樂之功邪？

translations.literal: Is this not the achievement of rites and music?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the power of rites and music?

sentences.zh: 夫禮樂有本、有文：中和者，本也；

translations.literal: Rites and music have root and form: centrality and harmony are the root;
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music have root and form: centrality and harmony are the root;

sentences.zh: 容聲者，末也；

translations.literal: bearing and sound are the branches;
translations.idiomatic: bearing and sound are the branches;

sentences.zh: 二者不可偏廢。

translations.literal: Neither may be one-sidedly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Neither may be neglected in favor of the other.

sentences.zh: 先王守禮樂之本，未嘗須臾去於心，行禮樂之文，未嘗須臾遠於身。

translations.literal: The former kings kept the root of rites and music and never for an instant let it leave their hearts; they performed the form of rites and music and never for an instant kept it far from their persons.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings held fast to the root of rites and music and never for a moment let it leave their hearts; they practiced the forms of rites and music and never for a moment kept them far from their persons.

sentences.zh: 興於閨門，著於朝廷，被於鄉遂比鄰，達於諸侯，流於四海，自祭祀軍旅至於飲食起居，未嘗不在禮樂之中；

translations.literal: It arose in the inner quarters, manifested at court, spread over districts and neighboring communities, reached the feudal lords, flowed through the four seas—from sacrifices and military campaigns down to eating, drinking, rising, and resting, nothing was ever outside rites and music;
translations.idiomatic: It began in the inner quarters, took shape at court, spread through districts and neighboring communities, reached the feudal lords, and flowed to the four seas—from sacrifice and war down to eating, drinking, and daily life, nothing lay outside rites and music;

sentences.zh: 如此數十百年，然後治化周浹，鳳凰來儀也。

translations.literal: After thus for tens and hundreds of years, then governance and transformation permeated all, and the phoenix came as an omen.
translations.idiomatic: Only after tens and hundreds of years of this did governance and transformation thoroughly permeate the realm, and the phoenix come as an omen of virtue.

sentences.zh: 苟無其本而徒有其末，一日行之而百日捨之，求以移風易俗，誠亦難矣。

translations.literal: If one lacks the root and has only the branches, practicing it one day and abandoning it for a hundred, to seek thereby to transform customs—truly that is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If one lacks the root and keeps only the outward forms, practicing them one day and abandoning them for a hundred, it is truly hard to expect customs to change.

sentences.zh: 是以漢武帝置協律，歌天瑞，非不美也，不能免哀痛之詔。

translations.literal: Thus Emperor Wu of Han established the Office of Harmonizing Pitch and sang of heaven's auspicious signs—not that it was not beautiful, yet he could not escape the Edict of Lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Wu of Han established the Office of Harmonizing Pitch and composed songs celebrating heaven's auspicious signs—not that these were not fine, yet he could not escape his Edict of Lamentation.

sentences.zh: 王莽建羲和，考律呂，非不精也，不能救漸台之禍。

translations.literal: Wang Mang established the Xihe office and examined pitch pipes—not that it was not precise, yet he could not avert the disaster of Jiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang established the Xihe office and tested the pitch pipes—not that this was not meticulous, yet he could not avert the disaster at Jiantai.

sentences.zh: 晉武制笛尺，調金石，非不詳也，不能弭平陽之災。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin made the flute measure and tuned bells and stones—not that it was not thorough, yet he could not quell the calamity at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin fashioned the flute measure and tuned bells and stones—not that this was not exhaustive, yet he could not quell the calamity at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝立四器、調八音，非不察也，不能免台城之辱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang established the four instruments and tuned the eight tones—not that it was not discriminating, yet he could not escape the humiliation of Tai Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang established the four pitch standards and tuned the eight tones—not that this was not discerning, yet he could not escape the humiliation at Tai Cheng.

sentences.zh: 然則韶、夏、濩、武之音，具存於世，苟其餘不足以稱之，曾不能化一夫，況四海乎！

translations.literal: If so, then the tones of Shao, Xia, Hu, and Wu all fully exist in the world—if one's remaining conduct is insufficient to match them, one cannot transform even a single man, how much less the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: If so, the music of Shao, Xia, Hu, and Wu all still exist in the world—yet if one's own conduct does not measure up to them, one cannot transform even a single man, let alone the four seas!

sentences.zh: 是猶執垂之規矩而無工與材，坐而待器之成，終不可得也。

translations.literal: This is like holding Chui's compass and square without craftsmen or material, sitting and waiting for vessels to be completed—it can never be attained.
translations.idiomatic: This is like holding Chui's compass and square without craftsmen or timber, sitting and waiting for finished vessels—it can never be done.

sentences.zh: 況齊、陳淫昏之主，亡國之音，暫奏於庭，烏能變一世之哀樂乎！

translations.literal: How much more when debauched and benighted rulers of Qi and Chen, with music of a perishing state, briefly played it in court—how could it change an age's grief and joy!
translations.idiomatic: How much less when debauched and benighted rulers of Qi and Chen had the music of a dying state played briefly at court—how could that change an age's grief and joy!

sentences.zh: 而太宗遽雲治之隆替不由於樂，何發言之易而果於非聖人也如此？

translations.literal: Yet Taizong hastily declared that the rise and fall of governance does not depend on music—how can speech be so facile and conclusion so quick to condemn the sages in this way?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taizong hastily declared that the rise and fall of governance has nothing to do with music—how can one speak so lightly and conclude so quickly that the sages were wrong?

sentences.zh: 夫禮非威儀之謂也，然無威儀則禮不可得而行矣。

translations.literal: Rites are not merely a matter of dignified ceremony—yet without dignified ceremony, rites cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are not merely a matter of dignified ceremony, yet without ceremony rites cannot be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 樂非聲音之謂也，然無聲音則樂不可得而見矣。

translations.literal: Music is not merely a matter of sound—yet without sound, music cannot be manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Music is not merely a matter of sound, yet without sound music cannot be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 譬諸山，取其一土一石而謂之山則不可，然土石皆去，山於何在哉！

translations.literal: It is like a mountain: take one clod or one stone and call it a mountain—that will not do; yet if all earth and stone are removed, where would the mountain be!
translations.idiomatic: It is like a mountain: one cannot take a single clod or stone and call it a mountain, yet if all earth and stone are removed, where is the mountain!

sentences.zh: 故曰：「無本不立，無文不行。」

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Without root there is no standing; without form there is no going forward."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: "Without root there is no standing; without form there is no going forward."

sentences.zh: 奈何以齊、陳之音不驗於今世，而謂樂無益於治亂，何異睹拳石而輕泰山乎！

translations.literal: How then, because the music of Qi and Chen was not validated in the present age, to say that music is of no benefit to order and disorder—what difference is there from seeing a fist-sized stone and belittling Mount Tai!
translations.idiomatic: How then, because the music of Qi and Chen did not prove itself in our own day, can one say music is of no use to order and disorder? What difference is there between seeing a fist-sized stone and belittling Mount Tai!

sentences.zh: 必若所言，則是五帝、三五之作樂皆妄也。」

translations.literal: If what you say must hold, then the composing of music by the Five Emperors and Three Five was all in vain."
translations.idiomatic: If what you say must hold, then the music composed by the Five Emperors and the Three Dynasties was all in vain."

sentences.zh: 君子於其所不知，蓋闕如也。」

translations.literal: The gentleman, regarding what he does not know, generally keeps silence."
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman, where he does not know, generally keeps silent."

sentences.zh: 惜哉！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 戊子，上謂侍臣曰：「朕觀《隋煬帝集》，文辭奧博，亦知是堯、舜而非桀、紂，然行事何其反也！」

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "I have read the Collected Works of Emperor Yang of Sui—the language is profound and vast, and he too knew to praise Yao and Shun and condemn Jie and Zhou—yet how contrary his conduct was!"
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "I have read the Collected Works of Emperor Yang of Sui. The language is profound and learned, and he too knew to praise Yao and Shun and condemn Jie and Zhou—yet how utterly contrary his conduct was!"

sentences.zh: 魏徵對曰：「人君雖聖哲，猶當虛己以受人，故智者獻其謀，勇者竭其力。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng replied: "Even if a ruler is sage and wise, he should still empty himself to receive others; thus the wise offer their plans and the brave exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied: "Even a sage ruler should empty himself to receive others, so that the wise may offer their counsel and the brave exert their strength.

sentences.zh: 煬帝恃其俊才，驕矜自用，故口誦堯、舜之言而身為桀、紂之行，曾不自知，以至覆亡也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yang relied on his outstanding talent, was proud and self-willed—thus he recited the words of Yao and Shun while acting as Jie and Zhou, never knowing it himself, until ruin came."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang relied on his outstanding talent and was proud and self-willed, so he recited the words of Yao and Shun while acting like Jie and Zhou, never knowing it himself, until the dynasty was overthrown."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「前事不遠，吾屬之師也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Recent events are not far off—they are a teacher for us!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Recent events are not far off—they are a teacher for us!"

sentences.zh: 畿內有蝗。

translations.literal: There were locusts within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts appeared within the capital region.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上入苑中，見蝗，掇數枚，祝之曰：「民以谷為命，而汝食之，寧食吾之肺腸。」

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the emperor entered the imperial park, saw locusts, picked up several, and prayed to them: "The people take grain as their life, yet you eat it—better eat my lungs and intestines."
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor entered the imperial park, saw locusts, picked up several, and prayed to them: "The people live by grain, yet you devour it—better devour my lungs and intestines instead."

sentences.zh: 舉手欲吞之，左右諫曰：「惡物或成疾。」

translations.literal: He raised his hand intending to swallow them. Those at his side remonstrated: "Unclean things may cause illness."
translations.idiomatic: He raised his hand to swallow them. Those at his side remonstrated: "Unclean things may cause illness."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕為民受災，何疾之避！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I bear disaster for the people—why should I avoid illness!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I bear this disaster for the people—why should I fear illness!"

sentences.zh: 遂吞之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he swallowed them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he swallowed them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蝗不為災。

translations.literal: That year, the locusts did not become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the locusts did not become a calamity.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕每臨朝，欲發一言，未嘗不三思。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Whenever I attend court, if I wish to speak a word, I never fail to think thrice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Whenever I attend court and wish to speak, I never fail to think thrice before I do.

sentences.zh: 恐為民害，是以不多言。」

translations.literal: I fear harming the people—that is why I do not speak much."
translations.idiomatic: I fear harming the people, and that is why I do not speak much."

sentences.zh: 給事中知起居事杜正倫曰：「臣職在記言，陛下之言失，臣必書之，豈徒有害於今，亦恐貽譏於後。」

translations.literal: Supervising Censor in charge of recording conduct Du Zhenglun said: "My office is to record speech; if Your Majesty's words err, I must write them down—not only might they harm the present, but they may also invite scorn from posterity."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor in charge of recording conduct Du Zhenglun said: "My duty is to record speech. If Your Majesty's words go astray, I must write them down—not only might they harm the present, but they may also invite ridicule from posterity."

sentences.zh: 上悅，賜帛二百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「梁武帝君臣惟談苦空，侯景之亂，百官不能乘馬。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Wu of Liang and his ministers talked only of the bitter emptiness of Buddhist doctrine; when Hou Jing's rebellion came, none of the hundred officials could ride a horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Emperor Wu of Liang and his ministers talked only of the bitter emptiness of Buddhist doctrine. When Hou Jing's rebellion broke out, not one of the hundred officials could ride a horse.

sentences.zh: 元帝為周師所圍，猶講《老子》，百官戎服以聽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was besieged by Zhou troops, he still lectured on the Laozi, and the hundred officials listened in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was besieged by Zhou troops, he still lectured on the Laozi, and the hundred officials listened in military dress.

sentences.zh: 此深足為戒。

translations.literal: This is deeply worth taking as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: This is a warning well worth heeding.

sentences.zh: 朕所好者，唯堯、舜、周、孔之道，以為如鳥有翼，如魚有水，失之則死，不可暫無耳。」

translations.literal: What I delight in is only the Way of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius—I regard it as birds having wings and fish having water; lose it and one dies—it cannot be briefly done without."
translations.idiomatic: What I hold to is only the Way of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius. I regard it as birds having wings and fish having water: lose it and one dies—it cannot be briefly done without."

sentences.zh: 以辰州刺史裴虔通，隋煬帝故人，特蒙寵任，而身為弒逆，雖時移事變，屢更赦令，倖免族夷，不可猶使牧民，乃下詔除名，流歡州。

translations.literal: Because Pei Qiantong, prefect of Chen Prefecture, was an old acquaintance of Emperor Yang of Sui and had been specially favored and entrusted, yet had himself committed regicide—though times had changed and amnesties had been repeatedly revised, sparing him from execution of his clan—he still could not be allowed to govern the people. An edict was issued striking his name from the rolls and exiling him to Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Pei Qiantong, prefect of Chen Prefecture, was an old acquaintance of Emperor Yang of Sui and had been specially favored and entrusted, yet had himself committed regicide—even though times had changed and repeated amnesties had spared him from execution of his clan—he still could not be allowed to govern the people. An edict was issued striking his name from the rolls and exiling him to Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 虔通常言「身除隋室以啟大唐」，自以為功，頗有觖望之色。

translations.literal: Qiantong often said "I personally removed the Sui house to open the Great Tang" and considered it his achievement, showing considerable air of resentment at unfulfilled expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong often said, "I personally removed the Sui house to open the Great Tang," and considered it his achievement, showing a clear air of resentment at unfulfilled expectations.

sentences.zh: 及得罪，怨憤而死。

translations.literal: When he was punished, he died of resentment and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When he was punished, he died of resentment and indignation.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，詔宇文化及之黨萊州刺史牛方裕、絳州刺史薛世良、廣州都督長史唐奉義、隋武牙郎將元禮並除名徙邊。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: an edict ordered that Yuwen Huaji's partisans—Niu Fangyu, prefect of Lai Prefecture; Xue Shiliang, prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Tang Fengyi, chief secretary of the Guangzhou military governor; and Yuan Li, Sui Wuya Langjiang—all struck from the rolls and exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, an edict ordered that Yuwen Huaji's partisans—Niu Fangyu, prefect of Lai Prefecture; Xue Shiliang, prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Tang Fengyi, chief secretary of the Guangzhou military governor; and Yuan Li, Sui Wuya Langjiang—all struck from the rolls and exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「古語有之：『赦者小人之幸，君子之不幸。』

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendant ministers: "An ancient saying has it: 'Amnesty is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attendant ministers: "An ancient saying has it: 'Amnesty is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's misfortune.

sentences.zh: 『一歲再赦，善人暗啞。』

translations.literal: Twice amnesty in one year, and good people fall silent.'
translations.idiomatic: Twice amnesty in one year, and good people fall silent.'

sentences.zh: 夫養稂莠者害嘉谷，赦有罪者賊良民，故朕即位以來，不欲數赦，恐小人恃之輕犯憲章故也！」

translations.literal: To nurture darnel harms fine grain; to pardon the guilty harms good people—therefore since my accession I have not wished to grant amnesties frequently, fearing that petty men would rely on them and lightly violate the laws!"
translations.idiomatic: To nurture darnel harms fine grain; to pardon the guilty harms good people. Therefore, since my accession I have not wished to grant amnesties frequently, fearing that petty men would rely on them and lightly violate the laws!"
